a.notes: Through the owner's lens this heat came down to line art plus glow. The two tour crosses that drew the page's structure with fine lines and kept a real lit tube (Trued, Yard Lit and Lit Manual, Dialled) lead clearly. Grafts that worked: Manual's dial taking Desk's patch-lead idea as one straight leader onto NOW, which looks native and is the most striking single line in the heat; Trued taking the main camp's rule heads and status foot and redrawing them as terminus-to-buffer track, which makes the main camp's frame into line art; Desk taking the tour's day numerals and rails; Dessau taking the tour's one-tube-per-page instrument grammar and making it Bauhaus circles. Grafts that read pasted: Settled's engraved seams and status foot, which calm it but drain its colour; Quote's cap rules, which colour it but add no structure; and Departures' T buffers, where the long To do rail to the Ready buffer is a buffer looking for a job. Camps: the tour brings the drawing (rails, leaders, yards, wires) that the owner has asked for since round 7. The main camp brings poster type, quote figures and cases, which help hierarchy, but its lines (Quote, Settled) still read as generic modern dashboards with a lit corner. The colour risk is now two-sided: Settled drained to bone and pewter, while Dessau's clay and tan tiles drift toward the warm browns the owner disliked. Cool steel and cyan companions (Trued), and Manual's sage, amber and heather kept small, are closest to supporting the green. On glow, Manual's dial, Dessau's dial and Desk's glass best restore the original halo and scanlines. Trued should give its resting foot lamp a steady dim glow so every page keeps one glowing dot.

scores.why: Has the original glow DNA, but it is the all-green Matrix page the owner asked to calm. There is no grounded colour, no line art and no structure to lead the eye.

The cased terminal keeps real CRT soul, and the rails are a start. The desk around it is close to colourless, its lower half is a grid of boxes, and the line language is thin next to this heat's best.

The track diagram the owner asked to see again: steel rails, ring stops and a lit now run, in cool steel and cyan. It is still boxy in places (the plates, the setup strip, the To do tray), and its lower half sits in frames.

The patch lead from the case into Coming up's NOW lamp is exactly the line art the owner loves, and the glass keeps its glow. The left column's lower half is still a tall boxed slab, and the wheat caps add little.

A better-balanced Desk. The terminal glass glows with scanlines and a lit 'plan.', the lead lands on NOW, the starters hang from a small rail and the day numerals lead every dated list. The case is still a heavy pewter slab, of the kind the owner called too dominant, and the wheat cap rules read as a warm accent rather than a supporting one.
A tidy count board with a good quote screen, but it reads as a generic dark dashboard of boxed panels. The line art is minimal and the CRT lives only in the one tube.

Unboxing helped. The quote screen with its four-week tape is real, glowing data, and the cap rules in section inks add measured colour. There is still almost no structural line art, the question title is a retired form, and To do and Plans read as plain modern tables.
Bold poster type, but 88% green and nearly monochrome: the green drowns everything the owner wanted grounded.

A big recovery. The 28-day dial is the most CRT-convincing instrument in the heat (halo, lit rim, rings carrying real day numerals), and every page now has its own tube drawing its own data. Colour is replaced, not removed. Against it: the clay and tan icon tiles drift toward the warm browns the owner rejected, and apart from Coming up's short NOW stem there is little line art joining the parts.

Signal Box's language on every page: a lit run from now to the tube, ring stops with day numerals, To do's lamp track and a moving-coil meter on Status, in steel and cyan. The plates and the setup strip are still boxed.

The fullest version of the line art the owner calls high style. Plates hang on thin leaders from their stops, every section opens on a terminus-to-buffer rule head, the house's other rooms are a siding yard of ring stops, and the page closes on a status line with steel leaders. The glow stays where the motif is: the Next up tube, the lit run and 'plan.'. Cool steel and cyan support the green rather than compete with it. The footer lamp is dark at rest, so Plans, To do and Settings lose their one lit dot.
Good grounded manual type with sage, amber and heather. The four-week slot glass is a tall, dim equaliser, and Home's lower half is plain lists.

The single most striking line in the heat: one straight lit leader drops from the glowing countdown dial onto Coming up's NOW lamp and carries on down the rail, and Lately added hangs its kinds from a rail of its own. The dial has scanlines, a halo and real plan days on its bezel. The colour is the most varied and grounded here. The leader is long and leaves an empty bay under the dial, and the kids' wishes line is a hole.
Vera's line with stops down the left and the dot-matrix board have soul. The page is heavily green (71%), and the board dominates the right column.

Real line art: the steel line from the box past the starters to a buffer, the wire into a board that glows with a big VT323 clock, and the 'Change here for' interchange in rose, amber and pewter rings. Green is still about 69%, To do's rail runs a long empty stretch to the Ready buffer, and 'headed' narrows the job.
The videotex map is calm and orderly, but greyish, close to monochrome bone. Its quote cords read pasted, and the CRT sits only in the small tubes.

Calmer and better joined: the short white-hot lead from the case into Plans' NOW lamp, a status line on the glass with a cursor, engraved seams. The colour has drained to bone and pewter (0.35% neon, little hue), and apart from the one lead there is little line art, so it reads as a quiet modern dashboard with a lit corner.

fixes.suggestion: KEEP the leaders from stops up to the hanging plates, the terminus-to-buffer rule heads on every page, the Around the house siding yard and the status-foot line. FIX: (1) Give the foot's lamp a resting light, a dim steady phosphor dot with a faint halo (not breathing) while Ready, so every page keeps one glowing dot; save the breathing for Answering. (2) The Next up tube's case is still a grey slab under the glass: thin it to a 2px graphite bezel with fine detail (screws, a vent row). (3) Home's lower half is all steel: give To do's track its amber lamps plus a sage NOW tick, and give the yard's stops their own small inks (heather for Wishes, sage for Memory) at low chroma, so the green is not alone. (4) Plans month: the date-strip glass and the grid's 'now' box both glow, so light only one. (5) Ideas' 'line from home' glass: its leader numerals are small, so set them at the day-numeral size.

KEEP the countdown dial with its plan days on the bezel, the one straight lit leader onto NOW, the Lately added kinds rail and the readout strip. FIX: (1) Fill the bay under the dial beside the leader: hang Next plan's caption lower, along the leader as a plate on a tick, or put the free-weekend arc's legend there, so the leader runs past content and not through empty ground. (2) Taper the leader after NOW and let it carry on faintly to Lately added's rail, so one line joins the right column. (3) The kids' wishes line is a hole: give it two ring stops (Maya, Theo) on a short rail with their counts. (4) Draw To do's rail on Home as on /tasks: a thin track with amber lamps, not a plain amber left edge. (5) Status: drop the 'FIG. 1' caption so the figure captions are one rule.

KEEP the scanlined terminal glass with 'plan.' lit and its afterglow cursor, the patch lead into NOW and the day numerals on every dated list. FIX: (1) The case is the heavy pewter slab the owner called too dominant: thin it to a hairline bezel with fine detail, and stop it at the starters so Ready and Wishes sit on the ground under a rule. (2) Replace the wheat cap rules with steel or cyan hairlines, or keep wheat only on figures. (3) Lately added is a full-width box: hang it from a rail like Coming up. (4) Status's eight-row 'On this page' list duplicates the bands, so make it a rail with stops.

KEEP the 28-day dial (lit rim from now to next, numbered rings) and one tube per page drawing that page's data. FIX: (1) Move the clay and tan kind tiles toward cooler, period inks (steel-cyan, heather, olive), since warm browns read off-motif. (2) Join the dial to Coming up with one drawn lead onto its NOW ring, so the poster gets one piece of line art. (3) Give the readout strip its own NOW tick. (4) The footer shape legend strip is empty weight, so drop it.

KEEP Vera's line from the box past the starters, the wire into the board and the interchange stops. FIX: (1) Cut green below about 60% by moving the board's dim rows to steel-cyan dot-matrix and keeping only the next row lit. (2) End To do's rail at its last task with a buffer, and set the Ready lamp in the footer, so the rail is not a long empty run. (3) Change the title back to a planning verb (see titles).

KEEP the short lead from the case into the NOW lamp and the glass status line with its cursor. FIX: bring colour back. The section tabs and kind words are too low-chroma to read, so give each cell's tab and head lamp a clear steel, wheat or heather ink. Put ring stops on the Plans and To do lists so the map has line art beyond one lead.

KEEP the quote screen with its four-week tape and 'one lit figure a page'. FIX: add structural line art (a rail with a NOW lamp under Coming up's hop rows, and the tape's NOW joined to the first row by a lead), and change the question title to an instruction.

a.titles: The best is "Tell Vera what to plan." (Trued, Yard Lit): it names who hears you, works as the box's label, takes in plans, reminders, ideas and wishes, and ends on the lit word with its full stop. "Give Vera something to plan." (Desk, Wired) is its near equal and, set on the glass with the cursor, the most CRT. "Hand Vera anything to plan." (Manual) works, though "hand" is a touch quaint. "Send Vera anything to plan." (Settled) collides with the Send button and reads as an instruction about the button. "Tell Vera. Let's plan." (Dessau) has the best poster voice and suits the bold type, but two sentences make a weak field label. "What should Vera plan?" (Quote) is a retired question form: it reads as asking the page to show the plan. "Tell Vera where we're headed." (Departures) fits its metaphor but narrows the job to outings and loses reminders and wishes, so it fails as FamilyDB's job.

a.notes:
The crosses beat their carried designs on every line, by +0.2 to +0.7 through this lens, and the soul has largely come back. Every 14b cross has a lit greeting, a hot key word and at least one tube that draws real data. Light is mostly wired to what it reports.

Grafts that worked:
- Manual took the main camp's round dial and a single leader, and dimmed every other NOW. It is the cleanest 'light where attention belongs' in the heat.
- Dessau rebuilt the dial as a 28-day rim lit from now to next. It is the most striking lit object, though too glowing at the title.
- Trued took the main camp's rule heads and status foot, and rebuilt setup as a siding yard with one lit ring. All of it is native to the track.
- Settled took Folio's glass status line with a cursor, which brings back the original's living terminal in a calm way.

Grafts that read pasted:
- Dessau's footer shape legend.
- Departures' long empty rail, run on to reach the Ready buffer.
- Slate-filled starter keys on Trued and Departures, which look like form buttons rather than stops.
- Quote's green-washed greeting card, where the light becomes a field rather than a figure.

Camps: the tour lines (Trued, Manual, Departures) bring the light into the structure as wires and tracks, so the whole page glows as one diagram. The main lines (Desk, Dessau, Quote) keep the light in one framed instrument. Desk's instrument is the most authentic terminal, but its desk stays lifeless. Trued's foot lamp going steel at rest is a soul risk: a page at rest should still have one pilot light.

scores.why: All the original light is here (halo, bloom, scanlines), but it is glare everywhere and monochrome. Nothing tells you where to look, and the page reads as the Matrix.
A real cased terminal with its question typed on the glass is strong CRT soul. But the desk beside it is a dead slate void, and the light stops at the case's edge.
The lit track from now to next and the Next up tube make the week glow as data. The greeting is a plain box, and the lower half of Home is unlit.
The patch lead from the case into the NOW lamp first joined machine and desk in light, and the dials on inner pages draw real data. Lately added and the lower left are lifeless and nearly colourless.

This is the most authentic terminal in the heat. The title is typed on the glass under Next up with a hot 'plan.' and a block cursor that fades to afterglow instead of vanishing, and a lit lead runs to a white-hot NOW. Every inner page's tube draws its own data (needle, ASCII late bars, countdown). The desk is still grey-on-graphite with almost no grounded colour, and the bottom band (Lately added) has no light of its own.
A bold poster with one round tube, but it is drained to 88% green, its waypoint rings sit on meaningless bearings, and below the poster the light feels decorative.

The 28-day dial is the most dramatic lit instrument in the heat: a rim lit from now to the next plan, an afterglow wedge and ringed day numerals that match Coming up. 'plan.' blooms huge in Outfit. The amber LATE 3 tube on To do and the glyph tube in the chat keep the machine alive on every page. The kit halo on a 7rem word is close to glare, and the footer shape legend is a costume strip.
The hot-cored 'plan.' over a scanlined pool is right, but the slot glass is a tall, half-empty equaliser, so the lit figure reports little.

The round countdown tube with a printed bezel, plan lamps and upright day numerals is a true period instrument, and one straight phosphor leader drops from its socket onto Coming up's NOW. That is the clearest case of 'light is wired to what it reports' in the heat, and every other NOW is dimmed to a fading trace, so the light is scarce and meaningful. The greeting sits in a soft green pool, and the page around it is a calm, grounded manual (wheat late, sage free weekend, kind squares). The long leader is bright for ~245px, and Ideas' square radar tube and Status's dial are small and a little detached.
The quote screen is lit and alive, but Coming up has no light of its own, and the household row is pasted.

The quote screen is filled with data (big '1 DAY', a THEN line, the four-week tape), Status opens on a huge lit $0.00 glass, and 'one lit figure a page' is a good law. The section caps in wheat, heather and steel ground the rest. But the greeting card is a large green-washed panel, so light spreads past the figure, and below it Home reads as three ruled columns with little phosphor life.
The bezelled glass and sized tubes are nicely CRT, but 'plan.' is stranded on a VT323 line, and the quote cords are ornament.

A glass case holding the sentence with a VT323 status line '4 plans · 3 late · Vera is listening▊' is a lovely return of the original's living terminal, and the chat composer repeats it. The short lead into NOW and the radar of plan days are honest light. The lower household index and the inner pages are mostly matte and quiet (the To do ASCII tube is good), and the title glass is small beside a page of plain lists.
The headlamp tube standing on the line with a power wire to its stop, and the lit run from now to the second stop, make the signal-box light real. The stretched graphite plates are empty.

The whole Home reads as one lit signal diagram at night. The greeting board sits in a soft phosphor pool with a hot 'plan.'. The Next up tube is the line's headlamp, the track is lit only from now to next, plates hang on leaders, and the Around the house yard lights one ring (setup) as its only lamp. Inner pages keep it: the Ideas line from home on glass, the month strip with one lamp, the Status meter, the chat's track with 'your turn'. At rest the foot lamp is steel, so some pages (To do, Settings) lose their live light, and the starter branch reads a little like grey form buttons.

The dot-matrix departures board, the radar and the spend meter read as real green tubes, and the lit wire from the box's ring into the board makes Home feel alive. But every board row glows at full strength, the filled green Add buttons are lit too, and green is 71% of the colour, so the light is less scarce than in the best of the field.

It is calmer without going dead: the board's rows are dimmed so the next plan and its big VT323 clock stand out, the Add buttons are steel, and the light is kept for the wire, the boards and the Ready lamp. The rail ending on a steel buffer opposite the 'Change here for' stop gives the station theme a finished feel. Removing the moving beam leaves the trace a little static, so I score it level with x14b-desk-cross (8.0), not above it.

fixes.suggestion: Keep: the greeting's phosphor pool and hot 'plan.', the headlamp tube on the line, the lit run from now to next, the leadered plates with drive figures, the siding yard with one lit ring, and the engraved seams. Fix: (1) Foot lamp: at rest give it a faint breathing sage pilot (about 30% phosphor, no halo) rather than a steel ring, so every page keeps one living light; go full white-hot only while answering. (2) Starter branch: drop the slate fills on the three starter keys and set them as stops on the branch (ring, words, dim destination), so they belong to the track rather than to a form. (3) To do on Home: give its NOW a lamp at the same strength as Coming up's, but only the lamp, so the section has its one light. (4) On the phone, lift the NEXT readout into the greeting glass above the box, so the lit next plan is in the first screen.

Keep: the round countdown tube (bezel ticks, plan lamps, upright numerals, free-weekend sage arc), the single straight leader onto NOW, the dimmed fading NOW traces elsewhere, the readout strip and the wheat late edges. Fix: (1) Shorten the leader: drop the dial so its socket sits about 80px above Coming up's head, and fill the column beside the title with the NEXT PLAN caption instead of empty ground. (2) Ideas: replace the square radar with the same round tube family (a 13rem round scope with numbered dots), so every page's tube is one instrument. (3) Status: make the cost dial larger and wire it with the same leader to 'What it has cost'. (4) Retire the FIG. 1 caption on Status so captions follow one rule.

Keep: the cased terminal with the title typed on the glass, the afterglow-blink cursor, the patch lead into a white-hot NOW, the inner tubes that draw data (needle, ASCII late bars, countdown dial), and the one-light-per-band rule. Fix: (1) Move 'Give Vera something to plan.' above Next up on the glass, since the prompt belongs above the tube's data. (2) Lately added: give its band a lamp (the newest row's ring lit), and put grounded kind colour in the rings (clay, sage, wheat, steel), because the desk is almost colourless. (3) Thin the graphite case's bottom half (From row, starters) so the glass dominates the column. (4) Month chips: take each plan's kind ink in their left edge rather than one dusk.

Keep: the 28-day dial with the rim lit from now to next and ringed day numerals matching Coming up, the amber LATE tube on To do, the chat's glyph tube, the readout strip and the section-ink squares. Fix: (1) Tone 'plan.' down to E1 at a smaller halo radius: at 7rem the kit halo smears into glare. (2) Drop the footer shape legend strip. (3) The two-sentence title reads as a slogan; try 'Tell Vera what to plan.' only if it is unused elsewhere, or keep 'Tell Vera, she'll plan.' in sentence case. (4) Status's meter is small beside a huge empty head: size it to the head's height.

Keep: the dot-matrix board with the big VT323 13:00, the wire from the box's ring, the four-week trace, Vera's line with the box as its first stop, and the Ready lamp on a buffer. Fix: cut To do's rail at its last task and put the Ready lamp in the page foot, since the 230px empty run of steel is lifeless. Drop the slate fills on the starters, and make the board's row hover steel rather than green so it does not compete with the wire.

Keep: the glass case holding the sentence with the VT323 status line and its cursor, the same glass on the chat composer, the short lead into NOW and the radar of plan days. Fix: make the case larger (about 60% of the column) so the glass is the page's lead; give the household index one lamp (the cell needing a look lit amber, the live one sage); and on Plans let the weekend inset grow, since 1.05rem VT323 in a cramped band loses the tube's legibility.

Keep: the quote screen full of data, the lit-figure law, the big lit $0.00 on Status and the section-ink caps. Fix: remove the green wash from the greeting card (graphite ground, a light pool only under the screen), give Coming up's lit '4' the E1 halo, and change the question title to an imperative ('Tell Vera what to plan.' or 'Give Vera something to plan.', whichever is free).

a.titles: Best are 'Tell Vera what to plan.' (Trued, Yard Lit) and 'Give Vera something to plan.' typed on the glass with a block cursor (Desk, Wired). Both are imperatives that name who hears you, and the lit 'plan.' is the job itself. On the glass the cursor makes the second the most CRT-souled setting. 'Hand Vera anything to plan.' (Manual) is a near equal: one clean line with the full stop lit. 'Send Vera anything to plan.' (Settled) reads well in its glass, but 'send' sounds like a channel. 'Tell Vera where we're headed.' (Departures) is the most atmospheric and fits the station, but it narrows the job to outings, not reminders or wishes. 'Tell Vera. Let's plan.' (Dessau) is a two-sentence slogan whose huge glow block is closer to glare than to a lit key word. 'What should Vera plan?' (Quote) brings back the retired question form: it reads as asking Vera for suggestions, not as a label for the box.

a.notes: Through the style lens, this round moved every line forward, and the crosses beat their carried designs everywhere. Dessau gained most: a data-true dial replaced the meaningless radar, colour came back and the poster stayed. Grafts that took: the patch lead and wire family carried into Manual (the dial's leader onto NOW) and Settled (the jack into NOW). The leader reads native in Manual because it hangs from the line's own countdown dial. Trued's taking main-camp unboxing and rule heads made it cleaner and consistent page to page. Dessau's dial (from the tour's countdown and waypoint ideas) is the best graft in the heat: it fuses the tour's 'figure drawn from data' with the poster's circle. Grafts that read pasted: Departures' terminus buffer stretched to a column's height (empty steel); Settled's household row is near identical to Quote's; Quote's tape and hero card still look like a generic dashboard hero. Camps: the tour finals bring the drawings (tracks, rails, boards), the main camp brings the head and the voice (poster, terminal, count figures). The two best here, Dessau and Trued, are each one camp with the other's best part. Convergence persists: rail-plus-NOW-lamp and 'Ready · gpt-6-luna · $2.00' feet appear on almost every design, so the field still looks alike in thumbnails. Signature devices (Dessau's poster and dial, Departures' board, Desk's case, Manual's dial and leader) are what make a line memorable, and they should be pushed, not softened. Phosphor's return: Dessau's dial rim and lit verb, Departures' board and Desk's glass with its cursor bring back the original's tube light best. Trued and Settled are tasteful but under-lit in a still.

scores.why: The original's tube light is real and charming, but it is one mood across the whole page: green boxes on black, no hierarchy of colour or type. Still the Matrix the family named.
A cased terminal is a memorable object and the meter is lovely. Next to this heat it reads boxed and greyer, though: slate panels stacked down a desk with little drawing between them.

The lit track from the now lamp is a true signature, and it draws the family's week. The plates are still boxed and the greeting is a plain card, so it is less finished than either of its descendants.
The patch lead from the case into NOW joins machine and desk in one drawing, a lovely idea. The desk around it is almost colourless, and the lower left has a hole.

Same terminal, better pacing. The day numerals with their stacked month and weekday are well typeset, the lead lands cleanly, and the phone now shows the week. Beside the terminal the desk is still steel boxes with wheat caps: tasteful, but timid in colour and voice.
The count-board figures give good scale contrast, but the page reads as a tidy dashboard of slate trays. The household strip is borrowed almost unchanged.

Unboxed columns under coloured cap rules, and a quote screen whose big lit '1 DAY' and tape are a real typographic moment. The hero is still a generic rounded card with a gradient wash, and the condensed two-line question looks handsome but feels like a stock headline.
The heat's boldest typography (lowercase Outfit poster), but its colour is drained to 88% green and the radar's rings sit on bearings that mean nothing.

The most memorable page in the heat. 'Tell Vera. Let's plan.' is set as a real Bauhaus poster in bone, with the lit verb, beside a 28-day dial whose rim glows only from now to the next ring: a figure that is both CRT and modernist. Section inks in squares and cap rules ground the body. Status and Chat lean back to mostly green, and the body rows are ordinary under so strong a head.
Signal-box track under a headlamp tube is a coherent, fresh drawing. The plates are stretched into empty graphite boxes, and the greeting is a framed card.

The boxes are off and the plates hang on leaders with the drive from home. 'Around the house' is a siding yard, and every head is a terminus-rule-buffer. It is the most consistent grammar on every page (the month strip, the Ideas line from home, chat as a line with 'your turn'). It feels like an engineered drawing more than a home, and the yard and status foot are thin, quiet lines that the squint loses.
The most varied colour in the field and an honest manual voice, but the slot-glass equaliser was a tall, half-empty figure.

The round countdown dial with lamps on plan days, printed bezel ticks, and one straight lit leader falling onto Coming up's NOW is the most striking single drawing after Dessau's dial. Lately added as a rail, with kind labels hanging left, is a fresh device. The leader is long over empty ground, and the right column under the dial goes dark.
A station at night is a lovely mood, with a dot-matrix board and a lit wire. It is heavy in green, and the rings on the form read as radios.

The board (a big VT323 13:00, dim leadered rows, a four-week trace) is still the most authentically phosphor object in the heat. 'Change here for' is charming wayfinding. But To do's rail runs ~230px into nothing to reach the Ready buffer, and the page is ~70% green: the right column is one long glow.
The switchboard map is a good idea, but its steel quote cords read as ornament, and 'plan.' is stranded alone on a VT323 line.

Calmer and well organised. The glass's status line '4 plans · 3 late · Vera is listening▊' is a delightful CRT touch, and the household row of big figures closes the page well. Otherwise the type is a plain condensed sans on bare ground, so it borders on stock dark-mode admin, and the radar beside Plans is decoration rather than a lead.

fixes.suggestion: KEEP the poster greeting (big bone Outfit, lit 'plan.'), the 28-day dial with its rim lit from now to the next ring, the section-ink squares and cap rules, and the readout strip. FIX: (1) When the next plan is tomorrow, the lit arc is a stub. Let the afterglow wedge carry the visible sweep (raise it toward 55%), or give the next ring a short echo trail, so the light reads in a still. (2) The three columns below the poster are ordinary rows. Give Coming up's rows the dial's ring style at the same scale and colour as the dial's rings, so the eye reads one system from figure to list. (3) Status and Chat fall back to near-monochrome green. Put the section inks (steel, clay, heather) on the 01/02/03 folios and the bank caps, and lose the green 'working' words in favour of the lamps alone. (4) The footer's shape legend (Light / The family's / The page / Late) is an empty strip: drop it or move it to Settings. (5) Month plan chips should take a kind ink where one exists.

KEEP the headlamp tube, the plates on leaders with the drive from home, terminus-to-buffer rule heads, and the Ideas line from home. FIX: (1) The greeting is the least drawn part of the page. Let the starter branch leave the box from the Send row as real track (not a separate panel), and put a small lamp at the junction. (2) 'Around the house' and the status foot vanish in the squint. Give each yard stop one figure at the numeral step (4 people, 3 to finish) and set the yard rail in its section inks, not all steel. (3) Give the Ready foot a faint steady lamp at rest (not lit, but a warm 30% dot), so every page keeps one light. (4) Warm the palette a little: one more grounded companion (wheat for To do's dates, heather for Lately added's rings), so it reads as a home, not only a signal box.

KEEP the round dial with plan-day lamps and upright numerals, the straight lit leader onto NOW, Lately added as a rail with kind labels hanging left, the readout row, and one lit line a page. FIX: (1) The leader runs ~245px past an empty right column. Move 'Next plan' and its caption under the dial, beside the leader, as stops on it (Oaks Park, then 9, 17, 24), so the line passes through content rather than ground. (2) Put the dial's bezel ticks on the same day numerals as Coming up's rows, at the same face and size. (3) Give Finish setting up and The kids' wishes one lamp each, so the lower left is not unlit. (4) Status's FIG. 1 caption: make figure captions one rule on every page.

KEEP the cased terminal with the title typed on its glass and the block cursor, the patch lead into NOW, and the day numerals with month/weekday stacks. FIX: (1) The desk is colourless steel. Give each band one grounded ink (wheat already caps it: add a sage for Coming up's numerals and heather for Lately added's kind rings). (2) Move the title above Next up on the glass, as usability asked last round, so the prompt leads. (3) Inner pages repeat the same dark case on the left with filters stacked in it, which reads heavy. On Plans and To do, shrink the case to the tube alone and let the filters sit on the ground.

KEEP the dot-matrix board (VT323 clock, leadered rows, four-week trace), the wire from the box's ring, and 'Change here for'. FIX: (1) Cut To do's rail to end at its last task and put the Ready buffer at a fixed short distance below it; never stretch steel to meet a height. (2) Cut green: dim the board's lower rows and the trace to 45%, and keep only 13:00 and the next tick at full phosphor. (3) Give the left column a grounded colour (the starters' left edges in section inks are a start; carry them into To do's numerals).

KEEP the quote screen with its big lit day figure and tape, and the unboxed columns under coloured caps. FIX: drop the gradient-washed rounded hero card and set the greeting on the ground like the columns. Change the title from a question to an invitation. Light Coming up's next row with the same figure as the screen rather than a separate green box.

KEEP the glass status line with its cursor and the household row of big figures. FIX: the type is stock condensed sans. Give heads a real display step (larger, with a figure) and make the radar beside Plans earn its place by drawing day rings that match the list's numerals, or drop it for a smaller tube.

a.titles: BEST: Dessau's 'Tell Vera. / Let's plan.'. It is the only title in the heat with a voice: two short poster beats, imperative then shared ('Let's' answers last round's complaint that Vera plans alone), and the lit verb lands last, right over the box. Trued's 'Tell Vera what to plan.' is the clearest label, a near equal, with the lit word and stop at the end. Manual's 'Hand Vera anything to plan.' is good: 'anything' is generous and 'hand' tactile. Desk's 'Give Vera something to plan.' still works, and on the terminal's glass with a cursor it is the most CRT setting, but it is the familiar line. WEAKER: Departures' 'Tell Vera where we're headed.' is charming in the station metaphor but reads as outings only: a reminder or a wish is not 'headed'. Settled's 'Send Vera anything to plan.' is serviceable, but 'send' is the button's word, not an invitation. FAILS: Quote's 'What should Vera plan?' is a question form the lessons retired. It asks the page to show a plan, and as the box's label it is backwards (the family should tell her, not be asked what she should do).

a.notes:
The crosses are clearly ahead of the anchors, and this time the gains are structural, not colour. Boxes are coming off almost everywhere (Trued, Quote and Settled went to seams and caps), and every top design now has a written rule for where light may fall: Manual's one lit stroke, Desk's one light per band, Quote's ink-versus-light figure law, and Trued's lamp at now. That rule is the main system gain of this round.

Grafts that took:
- Manual's dial taken back with Desk's patch-lead idea: the one straight lit leader onto NOW.
- Dessau's data-drawn round tubes on every page.
- Trued's main-camp rule heads and status foot, made track-native with terminus and buffer.
- Settled's jack lead and Folio's glass status line.

Grafts that read pasted or overdone:
- Trued's T buffer repeated at the end of every head link.
- Departures' rail stretched to reach a buffer.
- Quote's amber setup band.
- Dessau's footer shape legend.

The camps: the tour lines (Trued, Manual, Settled) bring drawings of the content, and the main lines (Dessau, Desk) bring frames and display type. Dessau is the main camp's big mover this round because it finally made its circles report real data.

Convergence is still visible: four Homes are now a dial or tube top right with a rail below. Each line's signature (Trued's track, Manual's dial and leader, Dessau's poster, Desk's case, Settled's glass status line) should be pushed, not softened.

Colour: Dessau and Manual use grounded inks best. Desk and Settled stay too bone.

Controls are consistent across the field: green focus rings, square ticks, dark selects. None of the details strips show a control fault worth separating the lines on.

scores.why: It has the real tube light, but nothing else is a system: a green wash on every box, card grids, no type steps, and the To do and Settings pages built as card piles. It is the yardstick for the light, not for structure.

The cased terminal column is a clear frame, and the ON THIS PAGE register with numbered bands carries across Status and Settings. The desk around it is nearly colourless, and boxed panels stacked inside boxed panels make the edges heavy.

The track grammar (terminus, ring stops, buffer, one lamp at now) is the clearest rule in the field. Graphite plates and slate trays still box most sections, and Status opens on a dense strip of lamps.

The patch lead from the case's socket into the NOW lamp joins the frame to the list honestly, and every list hangs from a rail. Ring-as-tick on To do, a hole under the wishes and the colourless desk hold it back.

A small, tidy step up: one numeral rule for days, one light per band, a two-kind label rule, and Lately added railed through both columns with an open stop at the end. The structure is the same as 14a. The Ideas page's left column of stacked chip buttons is clumsy, the Plans dial has the empty case of a tube placed in a corner, and the page is still almost monochrome apart from wheat caps.
With the costume off, the count board is legible: one figure per section head with a dotted leader. Rings and outlines in amber and boxed trays keep it heavy.

The law 'a figure that counts is ink, a figure that is live is light' is a real, portable system rule. Unboxed columns under coloured caps with 1px seams read well on Home, Status and To do. Finish setting up is still a full-width amber-edged band with a big amber 3, which reads as a warning. The quote screen is about half empty glass, and the tall condensed head type ('What should / Vera plan?') shouts against the calm columns.
Strong poster type and the readout strip, but drained to 88% green, with waypoint rings on bearings that mean nothing and every link underlined.

The biggest change in the heat. Every round tube now draws its own page's data: a 28-day dial lit from now to the next plan, a calendar leaf, a sqrt meter, LATE 3, nine segments for Settings. Section inks come back as square marks and caps, so colour has jobs again, and the readout strip, the 01/02/03 folios and the four shapes give it the strongest written rule set here. Against it: the Outfit display weight at 64px dominates every inner page, filled square kind chips on Ideas and Lately added edge toward confetti, the footer shape legend is still a strip, and the Status page's three folio columns are long and thin.
The Next up tube as the line's lit head with its power wire onto the first stop is the best Home figure of the carried set. Plates stretched to the rail leave empty graphite, and slate trays remain.

The most complete system in the heat. One rule-head component (terminus, name, count, rule, link, T buffer) opens every section on every page, engraved seams replace boxes, and only the greeting board and the tubes keep a frame. The plates hang on leaders, the Around the house yard folds setup in as a lamp, and Ideas' line from home and the Plans month strip are both rail drawings of real data. Light sits on the headlamp, the lit run to the first stop and the yard's setup lamp. Faults: T-buffer ticks at the end of every head and every link become a tic, the status foot is unlit at rest so most inner pages have no lamp, and the 4-target miss on Home.
Varied colour and good rails on every list, but the slot glass on Home was a tall, half-empty equaliser that replaced a better figure.

The countdown dial is back as one macro shared by Home and Plans, with day numerals on its bezel matching the rails. One straight lit leader drops from its socket onto Coming up's NOW lamp, and every other NOW is a fading trace: a strict, legible rule for where the light goes. The readout strip, engraved day numerals, the Lately added rail with kind labels in the margin, and To do's amber-edge late rows all hang together, and Status's wiring figure is the only diagram in the field that explains something. Held back by the busy Ideas filter area (chip row plus selects plus readout), the hole beside the kids' wishes, and a footer that is now a heavy two-cell block.
Vera's rail with the box as its first stop and the wire into the dot-matrix board is a fine idea. Green row hover and ring stops on form fields read as radios.

The buffer rule (every rail ends on a T, one mark per meaning) and the board with its four-week trace are solid, and the interchange row is a nice native close. But To do's rail now runs about 230px of empty steel down to the Ready buffer, a stretch made to fill space that every eye will catch. The board is still about 85% of the page's colour, and the condensed Archivo heads with tracked mono counts are two voices that never settle.
The two-tier map and household row are useful. Steel cords beside every figure are ornament, and 'plan.' was stranded on its own VT323 line.

Much calmer and more joined up. The jack on the case's bezel sends one short lead into the Plans NOW lamp, the status line on the glass ('4 plans · 3 late · Vera is listening▊') is a lovely CRT device, and engraved seams with section tabs replace boxes. The household index is the most useful foot on any Home. Against it: links underlined at rest everywhere (Maya 0, Theo 0, Every thing to do, Continue with Vera), large 1.1rem-plus row type that makes Home feel zoomed in, and a lot of plain bone with little colour beyond the green.

fixes.suggestion: Keep: the rule-head component on every page, engraved seams instead of boxes, plates on leaders with the drive fact, the headlamp tube with its lit run to the first stop, the Around the house yard with setup as its lamp, and Ideas' line from home. Fix: (1) Drop the T buffer after a head's link: end the rule at the link and keep the buffer only where a rail really ends (the Coming up track, the yard, To do's rail). Today every head ends '→ |', which reads as a typo. (2) Give the status foot a quiet lit state at rest: a small steady phosphor dot when Ready, breathing only while answering, so every page keeps one lamp. (3) Home: the four sub-44px targets are the inline Maya/Theo links in the yard and the head links; make each yard stop's whole cell the target and pad the head links to 44px. (4) To do on Home: the late lamps on the rail are amber dots identical to the lit-ring vocabulary. Make late a square or a short amber tick so a lamp stays a lamp. (5) Ideas: the line-from-home glass is good; let its numbered stops link to their rows.

Keep: the shared dial macro, the one lit leader onto NOW with every other NOW a fading trace (rule 19), the readout strip, engraved day numerals, the Lately added rail with kinds in the margin, and Status's wiring figure. Fix: (1) Home's lower left: the kids' wishes is one line under Finish setting up. Move wishes into the readout strip as a figure ('WISHES 0'), or set Finish setting up and wishes side by side, so the column ends level with Lately added. (2) Ideas: three control rows (SHOW chips, selects, then the kind chip row with counts) is too much. Make the kind chips the filter, drop the Kind select, and keep one row. (3) The footer is a heavy two-cell block with a vertical rule. Make it the same one-line colophon the other pages carry. (4) Status: give its wiring figure the dial's caption style and drop 'FIG. 1', so the figure captions are one rule. (5) The leader is long at 245px: try ending the welcome plate's lit band at the dial's foot and starting Coming up's head right there, so the leader is about 120px.

Keep: one round tube per page drawing that page's data (the 28-day dial, the leaf, the meter, LATE 3, the nine segments), the section ink squares and caps, the readout strip, the 01/02/03 folios on Status, and the poster title. Fix: (1) Bring the inner-page name down one step (from 64px to about 48px) so Plans, To do and Status don't open on a shout taller than their tubes. (2) Filled ink square chips on every Ideas row and every Lately added row become confetti: keep the square as a 10px mark and set the kind word in its ink, as Coming up does with rings. (3) Drop the footer shape legend (Light, The family's, The page, Late): the shapes explain themselves in place. (4) Status's three folio columns are long and narrow: put Who answers and Keys side by side and let Connected to run full width below, as a list. (5) Make 'Finish setting up' a quieter row: the boxed numerals 1 2 3 are big tiles at the same weight as the readout.

Keep: the cased terminal with the title typed on its glass, the patch lead into the NOW lamp, the one day-numeral rule, and Lately added railed through both columns ending on an open 'Add an idea' stop. Fix: (1) Colour: the desk is still bone on slate with wheat caps. Give each band's cap and count its section ink (steel for Plans, wheat for To do, heather for Ideas), as Dessau does, without adding glow. (2) Ideas: replace the case's stacked 3-column chip grid of kinds with a select or a single wrapped chip row; the case should hold the radar and search, not a control panel. (3) Plans: the dial case floats over empty ground beside the month. Put the next plan's name and the 'then' line under the dial as Manual does, so the case reports. (4) Status: the case's lamp register (1-8 with dots) repeats the bands beside it. Keep it as the contents and drop the duplicated 'Ready' foot under it.

Keep: the glass status line with the case's one cursor, the short jack-to-NOW lead, engraved seams with section-ink tabs, and the household index foot. Fix: (1) Remove underlines at rest from row and count links (Maya 0, Theo 0, Every thing to do, Continue with Vera, Sign-in and security): underline on hover, keep a colour or an arrow at rest. (2) Bring row type down a step: Home's 1.1rem bold rows make it feel zoomed. (3) Give the Plans radar's day marks the same numerals as the rows (it does), and drop the caption 'Each mark is a plan, by its day.' once the numerals match. (4) The Plans head's weekend inset glass is cramped: let it be the page's one tube and give it the height of the head row.

Keep: the wire from the box's ring into the board, the board with its four-week trace, buffers ending rails, and the Change here for interchange. Fix: (1) Do not stretch To do's rail to reach the Ready buffer: end the rail at the last task with its buffer, and put Ready in the left column's flow right after it (add content or shrink, never stretch). (2) Unify heads: condensed Archivo names with tracked mono counts ('4 COMING') are two voices; set counts in the body face. (3) Bring colour out of the board: give the starters' left edges and the kind rings their section inks at more weight, so the board stops being most of the page's colour.

Keep: the ink/light law for figures, unboxed columns under section-ink caps with 1px seams, and the next-plan numeral on the tiny tube. Fix: (1) Finish setting up: drop the amber edge and the large amber 3; set it as a quiet row with the next step as a link, since setup is not a warning. (2) Fill the quote screen or shrink it: today half its glass is empty between the THEN line and the tape. (3) Cut the head type a step and keep it on one line ('What should Vera plan?' at 2.25rem), or change the title (see titles).

a.titles: The best are Trued's "Tell Vera what to plan." and Desk's "Give Vera something to plan.". Both are imperatives that work as the box's label. Each names who hears you and ends on the lit word, and "something" or "what" takes in reminders, ideas and wishes. Desk's sits better as a system because it is typed on the glass with the site's one cursor. Trued's is shorter and sits on one line on desktop, with no orphan. Manual's "Hand Vera anything to plan." is a near equal: "anything" is generous, though "hand" is a little twee. Settled's "Send Vera anything to plan." doubles the Send button's verb, so the label and the action blur. Dessau's "Tell Vera. Let's plan." reads as a poster slogan, and "Let's" makes the planner us, not her: good as display type, weaker as a label. Quote's "What should Vera plan?" is a question form, which the lessons retire because it invites 'show me the plan'. Departures' "Tell Vera where we're headed." fits its metaphor, but it is about travel only and fails for a reminder or a wish.

a.notes:
The crosses beat their carried designs on every line except Departures, where stretching the To do rail to the Ready buffer cost more than the buffer system gained. Rows that start with a day numeral are now on nearly every line, and they read faster than the old date stamps.

Grafts that took:
- Trued: the main camp's rule heads and status foot. The rule heads made Trued's unboxed sections findable, and the foot gives every page a constant place for state.
- Dessau: the tour's honest dial and readout strip. The readout strip is the single best glance device in the heat.
- Manual: the main camp's round countdown, rebuilt as a shared dial macro used on Home and Plans.
- Settled: Folio's glass status line, which gives the state in words before the scan.
- Desk: the tour's day numeral, and square ticks taken back from the ring-tick failure.

Grafts that read as pasted:
- Departures' terminus buffers: a system rule that made empty rail.
- Quote's tiny lit '4' tube: a light placed by rule, not where attention goes.
- Dessau's shape-legend footer: a legend nobody needs.
- Trued's yard: native in drawing, but its inline links are small targets.

The camps:
- The tour lines win on route: one line through time that the eye follows.
- The main lines win on the head: title scale, the readout, the case.
- The top of the heat (Trued, Desk, Manual) joins both.

Lit-light discipline is good across the field: focus rings are consistent bright 2px green on every design, and nothing under 12px except Dessau's dial labels.

Risk: convergence. Rails with NOW, day numerals, and 'Vera … plan.' titles are on almost every design, so each line should protect its own signature as a way of finding things, not only as a look: Desk's case, Trued's line, Manual's dial, Settled's index, Dessau's poster, Quote's figures, Departures' board.

scores.why: Blurred, only the boxed greeting and the radar hold. Next up, setup and To do are all equal cards, and 42 of 55 Home targets are under 44px, so the eye has no route and the hand has small aims.

The case gives the eye a clear anchor and every target is 44px or more. But the title comes after Next up on the glass, and the right column is a stack of equal boxes, so Home takes reading rather than a glance.
Title, box, then the line of stops reads in that order, and the one lamp at now is unmistakable. The plates stretched to the rail read as empty graphite, and the tube sits below the fold on a phone.
The patch lead from the case to Coming up's NOW explains what the screen reports without words. The ring ticks on To do read as radios or lamps, and a hole is left under the wishes.

The lead lands on one lit NOW and the day numerals lead each row. To do is back to square ticks under a NOW rule. The case's foot now fills the hole (Ready, then wishes), and the starters are 44px rows. The title still sits under Next up on the glass, so the eye reads the plan before the job, and Ideas and Plans each count 6 targets under 44px.

Each column opens on a big figure, so the counts read at a glance. Coming up's cell has no light and the household strip is dense, so the next plan is found by its numeral, not by the eye being led there.

Unboxed columns under coloured caps squint well, and the quote screen's '1 DAY' plus a tape of the four weeks answers 'what's next' in one look. The page's one lit figure is the tiny '4' tube, which loses to the big screen and the amber '3' of setup. The ticker says 'Answering' where a count would scan.
The poster title is the strongest sight line in the heat. The radar's rings on meaningless bearings mislead, and the 88% green drains the cues that set apart what each area does.

The dial is now honest: the day rings sit at days-out angles and the lit rim runs from now to the next plan. The readout strip (Today, Plans 4, To do 4, Late 3, Ideas 12) is the best glance line on any Home, and the setup steps are numbered keys. Against it, the dial's VT323 labels are tiny, the lit arc is short when the plan is tomorrow, and 'Let's plan.' splits the label into two sentences.
The readout and the rails are clear, but the slot-glass equaliser is a tall half-empty figure with 10px numerals that needs decoding.

Title, then box, then chips, then a readout of counts: the reading order is textbook. The dial's caption names the next plan beside it, and To do's NOW and late edges scan at once. The single lit leader runs 245px through dark ground and seems to point at nothing until you reach NOW. Chat has 2 small targets.
The lit wire from the box into the board ties asking to answer. Green row hovers compete with the wire, and the form's ring stops read as radios.

The board is the most legible next-plan readout here (13:00 big, then the rows, then the trace), and the starters are full-width 44px bars. Against it, To do's rail runs about 230px of empty steel to reach the Ready buffer, the left column reads as a long ladder, and 'where we're headed' leaves out reminders and ideas.
The household row is very usable. The steel cords beside every figure are noise, and 'plan.' alone on its own line reads as a broken label.

The glass status line ('4 plans · 3 late · Vera is listening') tells the state before you scan, and the short lead lands on Plans' NOW. Two tiers end level and the household row is a real index with figures. The Plans radar ('each mark is a plan, by its day') is a figure that needs its caption, and on the phone Plans only starts at the fold.

The Next up tube stands as the line's head with a wire to its stop, and the line's left-to-right time is instantly read. The plates stretched to the rail leave dead graphite, and the phone's tube falls below the fold.

The clearest route in the heat. A big one-line title, then the box with Send, then the starters on their branch, then the week as a line with plates on leaders over their stops (now with the drive), the lit run from now to the next stop, then To do and Lately added under rule heads, the yard, and a status foot. On the phone a one-line NEXT readout is in the first screen. Faults: the next plan is shown only in the tube and has no plate on its own stop, 4 small inline targets in the yard (Maya, Theo, the setup link), and the setup lamp in the yard is easy to miss.

fixes.suggestion: Keep: the one-line title over the box, the starter branch, the plates on leaders with the drive, rule heads, engraved seams, the yard and the status foot, and the phone's NEXT readout. Fix Home: give stop 4 (the next plan) a plate of its own, or a short lit label 'Oaks Park · 13:00' under its numeral, so the line names every stop and the tube is not the only place the next plan is written. Make the yard's kid links and setup link 44px tall (pad the whole stop, as already done for the stop link). Let the setup stop's lit ring carry a one-word label ('Set up: 3 left') at the same weight as the other stop names, so it is seen as the yard's action. Keep the foot lamp green at rest in a dimmer 'Ready' state rather than all steel, so every page keeps one live light.

Keep: the lead from the case's socket to NOW, the day numeral leading every row, square ticks with a NOW rule on To do, the case foot (Ready, wishes), and the 44px starter rows. Fix: move 'Give Vera something to plan.' above Next up on the glass (prompt, then the tube's data), or put Next up below the box, so the eye meets the job before the plan. Bring Ideas' kind chips and Plans' view and month keys to 44px (6 under on each). Give Status a 'here' state again with one lit lamp in the contents plate, not two. Add sage or wheat to the desk side (the Coming up cap, the Lately added kind words) so it is not near-colourless.

Keep: title, box, chips and the readout strip as Home's head; the dial with numerals on its bezel and its caption beside it; one lit stroke a page; unboxed rails. Fix: shorten the leader by putting Coming up directly under the dial (a right column that starts with the dial and continues into its list) so the lit line is 60-90px and visibly lands on NOW. Swap To do and Coming up on Home so the dial sits above its own list. Give the chat's two small controls 44px. Fill the dark ground under the dial with the free-weekend line and 'then 9, 17, 24' as links.

Keep: the glass status line, the short lead from the case into Plans' NOW, the ending tiers and the household index with figures. Fix: on Plans, swap the radar for the dial or a straight 28-day strip with day numerals (the radar needs its caption to be read). On the phone, put the next plan's row (or the glass status line naming it) in the first screen. Give the household cells' lamps a legend in the foot, or drop the ones without meaning.

Keep: the poster title scale, the readout strip under the box, the honest 28-day dial, and numbered setup keys. Fix: set the title as one sentence ('Tell Vera, she'll plan.' or 'Tell Vera what to plan.') so it works as the box's label. Raise the dial's ring numerals and week labels to at least 16px and print the next plan's name and time large inside the hub. Draw the lit arc with a minimum length (and the afterglow wedge) so tomorrow still reads. Drop the shape-legend footer: the shapes should explain themselves.

Keep: unboxed columns under coloured caps, big figures by each head, the quote screen with its tape, and fig-live for one lit figure. Fix: make the lit figure the quote screen's own countdown, not the tiny '4' tube under Coming up, so the page's one light is where the eye already goes. Change the household Status cell to a count ('6 working'). Mute the setup strip's amber '3' to the label ink so it does not outshout the plans. Consider the imperative title, which reads as a label, over the question.

Keep: the wire from the box ring into the board, the big clock on the board, the 44px starter bars and the trace. Fix: stop To do's rail at its last task and put the Ready buffer straight under it; don't stretch the rail 230px. Bring the title back to one that covers reminders and ideas ('Give Vera something to plan.' is taken; try 'Tell Vera what's next.'). Mute the board's row hover so it does not compete with the wire.

a.titles: The best two are 'Tell Vera what to plan.' (Trued, Yard Lit) and 'Give Vera something to plan.' (Desk). Both are imperatives that work as the box's label, both name who hears you, and both end on the lit verb. Trued's sets on one line in the largest type, ahead of the box, so it is read first. Desk's sits under Next up, so the eye meets it second. 'Hand Vera anything to plan.' (Manual) and 'Send Vera anything to plan.' (Settled) are nearly as good: 'anything' invites reminders and ideas. 'Send' fits a box that has a Send button. 'Hand' is a little odd, and Settled's break before 'to' is set well. 'What should Vera plan?' (Quote) reads as a question to the family, so it works as a label, but it can also be heard as asking the page to show Vera's plan. 'Tell Vera. Let's plan.' (Dessau) is the strongest poster but two sentences: the box's label is only 'Tell Vera.', and 'Let's plan' says nothing about what to type. 'Tell Vera where we're headed.' (Departures) fails: it narrows the job to outings, and 'Remind me to…' has nowhere to go under it.

a.notes:
Grafts that worked typographically:
- Waypoint's readout strip on Dessau and Manual. It is a dotted-leader line of label and figure, and it reads as native type on both.
- The contents-line head with a light figure. It is now on Quote, Settled and Dessau, and it is the best shared device.
- Desk's two label kinds. This was a system fix rather than a graft.

Grafts that read as pasted:
- Trued's DM Mono drive figures inside sans plates.
- Departures' mono micro-cap counts beside condensed heads.

The camps have converged on condensed display heads and light numerals. The main camp (Quote, Dessau) brings the stronger written scale. The tour (Manual, Trued) brings tighter list typesetting: date stacks and rails. The best next step would put Dessau's display scale and readout over Quote's figure law, with Manual's date stack in every dated list.

Every cross beat its carried design through this lens.

scores.why: One loose sans in roughly two sizes. Heads are barely heavier than body, the dates sit in stacked boxed chips, and nothing is tabular. Pleasant and legible, but it has no hierarchy or scale to speak of.
It has a real scale and mono figures in the lists, and the glass title is a good typeset moment. Its small mono caps are over-used, and the desk type is thin and grey.
Archivo heads with DM Mono times give a clear two-face system. The question title is weak, and the small tracked labels crowd the plates.

The VT323 title on the glass with its cursor is lovely. Coming up's light numerals with a stacked month and weekday, leaders and mono times line up well. The desk's heads are still a little timid against the glass.

'to plan.' is held together, and the day numerals are one rule with a phosphor underline under the figures themselves. Labels are now split into two clean kinds (sentence-case sans against tracked mono column heads), which is a real system gain. The wishes line ('Maya 0 · Theo 0 open') sets awkwardly, and the case foot type is crowded.
Condensed titles with a figure and a stacked legend make a strong count-board hierarchy. The boxed trays and the busy household row dilute it.

This is the most complete type system in the heat. Condensed display heads carry light condensed figures in each section's ink. Contents-line heads use dotted leaders, column heads are sentence case, and leading noughts are dropped from dates ('Thu 1 Oct'). The tabular mono times align, and the chat-head line keeps one face and one x-height. Status reads like a well-set financial page. To do's names wrap to two lines in a narrow column, and the featured Lately added entry breaks the list's rhythm.
The poster scale is bold, but the lowercase display title and page names ('status', 'things to do') read as a mannerism. The body is underset against the display.

The best display typography in the heat. Outfit sentence-case names at a true poster size and the 01/02/03 folios in light numerals give an unmistakable hierarchy. The readout strip (TODAY ··· Sat 3 Oct, PLANS ··· 4) is beautifully set, and Coming up's diary line ('SUN 4 OCT · in 2 days') is right. 'Change a key' is a stray tiny bold, the micro-legend in the footer is noise, and three-line row stacks loosen the rhythm.
Plex throughout gives a manual's discipline, with engraved day numerals and a readout. The slot glass's 10px numerals and the long empty runs hurt it.

The single-line condensed title with the full stop in the lit run is the best-measured title in the heat. Day numerals with stacked month and weekday caps are consistent across To do, Coming up and the dial. Times sit right-aligned over relative words, and right-set kind labels hang on Lately added's rail like a book's marginalia. The colophon foot is typographically handsome. The dial's numerals are small, and the caption block beside it is a little stacked.
A clean Archivo and DM Mono pairing, with plates that carry a time well. 'Needs a' makes the title clunky, and the plates' type floats in empty graphite.

The rule heads (terminus, name at the 24px step, count, rule, buffer) are a fine typographic device on every page. The title reads on one line, and the drive figures are set tabular with dimmed units. But dates mix three faces ('4' in light sans, 'Oct Sun' in mono), the slashed-zero DM Mono '0' in 'Maya 0' reads as Ø, and mono units sit inside sans phrases in the plates.
The board's dot-matrix VT323 is good, but the desk type is generic and the tracked micro caps are too small.

The condensed title with its curly apostrophe is well set, and the board's VT323 clock and leader rows are a real piece of typesetting. The heads' '4 COMING' and '12 IDEAS' are tracked mono micro caps too small to pair with the condensed heads, the left column ends in a long empty run, and the 'Change here for' stops set three sizes in a small space.
The contents-line heads with light figures are good. 'plan.' stranded on its own VT323 line breaks the sentence, and the steel cords crowd the figures.

One condensed sentence on the glass with a nowrap 'to plan.' is fixed. The 0.875rem type floor tidies every small label. The household index (Wishes ··· 0 open, Family ··· 4 people) is the clearest figure-and-unit setting on any Home here. The title's halo lies on bone words that are not lit, so it softens their edges, and the Plans heads' stacked 'coming / next tomorrow' legends are cramped beside big light figures.

fixes.suggestion: Keep: condensed heads with light figures in section ink, contents-line heads with dotted leaders, sentence-case column heads, dates without a leading nought, and one lit figure a page. Fix: Home To do needs a wider name column (or the due words on their own line), so names stop wrapping beside 'was due'. Set Lately added's first entry as a row like the others, or give it the section's big figure instead of a larger name. Keep the 'working / 7 off' legend beside the Status figure on one baseline, so the stacked legend's x-height matches the subtitle. Since the question forms are retired, consider 'Tell Vera what to plan.' set on two condensed lines, broken before 'to'.

Keep: sentence-case Outfit names, the 01/02/03 light folios, the readout strip with dotted leaders, and the diary line 'SUN 4 OCT · in 2 days'. Fix: set 'Change a key' and the other bare links at the body's size and weight. Drop the footer shape legend. Tighten each Coming up row to two lines, and put the numeral ring on the first line's baseline. Make the display title's leading tighter still (about 0.9), and track it slightly negative at 96px so 'Let’s plan.' sits as one block. Set the Status rows' 'working/off' words as tabular small labels in one column, so they align across the three columns.

Keep: the one-line condensed title with the stop in the lit run, the engraved day numeral with stacked month and weekday caps, the right-aligned time over relative words, and the colophon foot. Fix: set the dial's day numerals and NEXT IN at least 14px, and use one face (VT323 or Plex Mono, not both). Set the caption beside the dial as a two-line block (name, then 'Sun 4 Oct, 13:00 · in 2 days'), and fold 'then 9, 17 and 24 Oct' into the second line. Lately added's right-set kind labels should all carry the same dot weight. Settle 'FIG. 1' one way on every page.

Keep: the VT323 title on the glass with 'to plan.' held together, the underlined day numeral rule, the two label kinds and the leader rows. Fix: reset the wishes foot as 'Wishes  Maya 0 · Theo 0 open', with the figures tabular and one unit. Give the desk heads (Coming up, To do, Lately added) one step more size or weight, so they hold their own against the glass. Align To do's two-line margin dates on the right with the month in tabular figures.

Keep: the rule heads and the one-line 'Tell Vera what to plan.'. Fix: set each date in one face. Use the light sans numeral with a sans month and weekday (or all mono), never both in one date. Use DM Mono's plain zero (or tabular sans) so 'Maya 0' does not read Ø. In the plates' foot, set units in the same face as the figures.

Keep: the type floor, the household index and the one-sentence glass title. Fix: take the halo off the unlit 'Send Vera anything' so only 'plan.' glows. Lay the stacked head legends ('coming / next tomorrow') out on one line after the figure. Align the Plans rows' times into one tabular column, with the relative words underneath.

Keep: the board's VT323 clock, the leader rows and the condensed title. Fix: replace the tracked mono micro caps in heads ('4 COMING') with sentence-case sans at the body's small step. End To do's rail at its last row, not 230px later. Set the 'Change here for' stops' names and states at one size.

a.titles: The best titles are Trued's 'Tell Vera what to plan.' and Desk's 'Give Vera something to plan.'. Each names who hears you and ends on the lit verb, and both set cleanly: Trued on one line, Desk on the glass with 'to plan.' held together. Manual's 'Hand Vera anything to plan.' comes a close third and has the best measure, one line with the stop in the light. Settled's 'Send Vera anything to plan.' works, but 'send' is mechanical. Dessau's 'Tell Vera. Let’s plan.' is the strongest typographic object, a poster couplet, but 'Let’s' blurs who plans. Quote's 'What should Vera plan?' sets beautifully in condensed type, but it is a question form the lessons retired, and it asks the page rather than labelling the box. Departures' 'Tell Vera where we’re headed.' fails the job: it narrows FamilyDB to trips, and reminders and wishes fall outside it.

a.notes: Every cross beat its carried design for usability except Departures, where greyed primaries and the empty rail to Ready cost more than the buffer system gained. Grafts that worked for usability: the steel siding yard on Trued (it puts Wishes, Memory, Family and the next setup step on Home in one line; the household-row idea in its own drawing), the round countdown dial on Manual (the next plan named beside the figure is the fastest answer to 'what's on'), and on Desk the square tick plus the rail's open 'Add an idea' stop. Settled's engraved seams and status foot calmed the page without hiding anything. Grafts that read pasted or cost a task: Quote moved Add to do into a dropdown (a removal that hides the primary). Departures took buffers from the main camp's foot and paid with empty steel. Dessau's tubes on every page are true now, but the poster still costs the Home link and a Late filter. Missing task paths to fix across the field: a Late filter on To do (Desk, Dessau), Home in the bar (Dessau), a green add button on every list page (Departures, Quote's To do), and the next plan in the phone's first screen (Settled, Trued's plates). The camps have met. The tour lines (Trued, Settled, Manual) lead on getting the day's tasks done at a glance, and the main lines (Desk, Quote) lead on clean, readable lists. The best usability is where a tour line took a main-camp frame (Trued's foot and rule heads, Settled's seams), as the 14a lesson found. Settings is the one page where all seventeen are equally usable. Settled's raised 14px label floor is worth making the standard for tired eyes on a phone.

scores.why: Every task works, but Home is a stack of equal-weight boxes: the next plan sits below the setup card, To do is a grid of cards with three folded 'Edit, complete, or snooze' per task, and nothing tells you at a glance what is late.

Clear terminal-plus-desk Home with To do and Coming up readable at a glance, but To do drops the Late filter, the To do page's left tube takes a third of the width for four rows, and the lower left of Home is a hole beside Lately added.

The track puts this weekend's stops in one row with day numerals, and To do has Open/Late/Done tabs with a NOW line through the list. The plates are cramped (9-10px meta), the starters are a narrow column, and setup takes a whole band of Home.

Next up tube at full height and the line of plates make 'what's on this weekend' a one-look task, and To do keeps the Late tab. Plates stretched down to the rail leave empty graphite, and on the phone the tube falls below the first screen.

The best set of Home tasks in the heat. The box comes first with the starters beside it. The plates now name the drive from home. To do shows its three late rows in amber over a NOW line. One 'Around the house' line holds Wishes per kid, Memory, Family and the next setup step. Every inner page keeps Late, All ideas/Restaurants and a green primary. Costs: four yard links under 44px, and the foot's Ready lamp is unlit at rest.
The patch lead ties Next up to the list well, but the ring-as-tick on To do reads as a radio or lamp, there is a hole under the kids' wishes, and the title sits under Next up on the glass.

The ticks are squares again and Coming up is now a clean numeral list with times and 'in 6 days'. Lately added hangs both columns from the rail and ends on an 'Add an idea' stop, and the phone opens on Next up. To do still has no Late filter (Open/Done/Cancelled/All only), and the To do and Plans side tubes push the list to two thirds of the width.
The figure-led heads make counts fast to read and the household row is a good jump table. The heavy amber setup rings fight the content, and Coming up has no light to mark the next plan.

Home is very legible: a quote screen whose '1 DAY' answers 'what's next', three typeset columns, a household row with Settings '3 to finish'. Ideas has kind chips with counts beside All/Restaurants, the best filter in the heat. To do's 'Add something to do' is now a grey dropdown in the filter row rather than a primary, and the month's plan chips are dim slate that tired eyes will miss.

Big poster names and the readout strip read fast, but there is no Home in the bar and every link is underlined. The radar's waypoint rings look like data and are not, and colour is drained to 88% green.

Every tube now draws real data (28-day dial, LATE 3, 8 of 9), and Coming up rows carry the date and 'in 2 days'. Status's 01/02/03 columns are clear. Home is still missing from the bar (only the wordmark gets you there). To do has no Late tab even though LATE 3 is printed beside it. Ideas' drive column is long prose ('about 2 h 10 min south of home') that is hard to scan. The Settings index runs tiny type down long leaders.
The rails and the To do-first Home are strong for the daily tasks. The slot glass equaliser on Home is tall with 10px numerals and tells a tired reader little.

The round countdown dial with the next plan named beside it ('Oaks Park roller rink, Sun 4 Oct 13:00, then 9, 17 and 24') is the clearest 'what's next' figure in the heat, and it sits above the fold on the phone. Home's readout (NEXT · PLANS · TO DO · LATE · IDEAS) is one glance, and To do has a Late tab and 'No active reminder' per row. The NOW trace through the month grid runs under the plan names and reads as a strike-through. The 245px leader is long.
The box as the line's first stop and the board beside it work well, but ring stops on the form fields read as radio buttons and the green row hover competes with the wire.

Home still reads well: the box, starters with destinations, To do with numerals, the board with the next time big, the kids' wishes per kid. Inner-page primaries (Add an idea, Add something to do) are now grey outlines, harder to find. Plans has no add button, and its month falls below a big board. To do's rail runs 230px of empty steel down to Ready. The title fails for reminders.
The two-tier map and the household index make every page one click from Home. 'plan.' stranded on its own line reads as a broken label, and the steel cords beside every figure are noise.

The best at-a-glance Home for a first-time user: box, starters with 'usually To do', Plans with times and 'in 6 days', To do with 'was due' in amber, Ideas with '2 restaurants to try' as a link, and a household row that puts Sign-in and security's needs-a-look on Home. Labels are raised to 14px, and Settings lists needs-a-look first. Ideas folds Status/For behind 'More filters' (one extra click), and on the phone the next plan sits about a screen and a half down.

fixes.suggestion: Keep: the box-first Home with starters beside it, the plates with the drive, the To do NOW line, the 'Around the house' yard with the next setup step as a link, the Late tab, and the unboxed Find on Ideas. Fix: make each yard stop at least 44px tall, with the whole stop as the target, not only the name. Raise the plate meta (kind word, whom, drive) from about 11px to 13px and the To do margin dates from 12px to 13px. Light the foot's lamp steady at rest when the model is reachable, and breathe it only while answering, so 'Ready' never reads as off. On the phone, move Coming up's first plate above the starters, or make the NEXT readout tappable to Plans with its time and day in 14px.

Keep: the two-tier map, the household row with needs-a-look on Home, the 14px label floor, Settings listing what needs a look first, 'Continue with Vera', and '1 with no date' on To do. Fix: on Ideas, show Status and For inline instead of behind '+ More filters'; the family looks for 'planned' and 'for Maya' often. On the phone, put Plans' next stop before the starters, or give the glass status line the next plan ('next Sun 13:00 Oaks Park'). On Plans, the 'Connect the calendar' primary beside the head competes with nothing to add; put 'Add a plan' first and connecting second.

Keep: the square ticks (the 14a ring-ticks were the line's worst usability fault), the numeral list in Coming up, the rail's 'Add an idea' open stop, and Next up first on the phone. Fix: add a Late tab to To do's Show group, since the page prints '3 late' in the head and there is no way to filter to them. Move 'Give Vera something to plan.' above Next up on the glass so the box's label sits next to the box. Shrink the side tubes on To do and Plans to 16rem, or put them above the list on screens under 80rem, so the list gets the width.

Keep: the dial with the next plan named beside it, the one-line readout, To do before Coming up on Home, the Late tab, and the setup steps as numbered links. Fix: in the month, end the NOW trace at today's cell edge or run it in the gutter under the week, not across the plan names, which reads as crossed out. Shorten the leader by putting Coming up's head level with the dial's foot. Fill the 150px under the dial with the 'Lately added' rail rather than leaving ground.

Keep: the kind chips with counts on Ideas, the household row, the '1 DAY' quote screen and the three typeset columns. Fix: put 'Add something to do' back as a green primary at the head of To do; a dropdown in the filter row is not where a first-timer looks. Give the month's plan chips bone text on slate at full contrast. Show the status lamp count in the household row ('6 working') as the designer notes.

Keep: the data-true tubes (28-day dial, LATE 3, 8 of 9), Coming up with the date and 'in 2 days', and Status's numbered columns. Fix: put Home in the bar on desktop and phone. Make the To do readout's 'LATE 3' a link that filters to late, or add a Late tab. Set Ideas' drive as a figure column ('27 min S') like the other lines. Raise the Settings index's state text to 14px and drop the leaders.

Keep: the box as the line's first stop, the board with the next time big, the per-kid wish rows and the 'Change here for' interchange. Fix: make Add an idea and Add something to do green primaries again, and add 'Add a plan' on Plans. End To do's rail at its last task and put Ready in the shared foot instead of a 230px empty run. On Plans, shrink the board so the month starts in the first screen. Change the title (see titles).

a.titles: The best two: 'Tell Vera what to plan.' (Trued, Yard Lit) and 'Give Vera something to plan.' (Desk, Wired). Both are instructions that name who hears you, work as the box's label, and take in reminders, ideas and wishes. 'Send Vera anything to plan.' (Settled) and 'Hand Vera anything to plan.' (Manual) are near equals: 'anything' invites, though 'send' and 'hand' are a little odd for typing a sentence. 'What should Vera plan?' (Quote) works as a label, but a question can be read as the page offering to show a plan, and it is weaker for 'remind me to'. 'Tell Vera. Let's plan.' (Dessau) splits the instruction from the box into two sentences, and 'Let's' leaves unclear who does the planning. 'Tell Vera where we're headed.' (Departures) fails: it fits an outing but not a reminder, a wish or a to-do, so a first-time user would not think to type 'remind me to renew library cards' under it.

a.notes: Every cross beats or matches its carried design except Departures, which matched it at best. Grafts that took: Manual's dial with the leader straight onto NOW (Sill Line's stem done right this time), Trued's rule heads, engraved seams and status foot from the main camp, Desk's tour-style rail through Lately added, and Dessau's real-angle dial (the waypoint failure corrected).
