Grafts that read pasted: Departures' 'every rail ends on a buffer', which forced a 230px dead rail; Settled's glass status line, which made its glass a Desk copy; Quote's tube tape is fine but its setup rings are still Sill's amber rings; Dessau's afterglow and legend strip. Convergence is still the skeptic's main worry: Desk, Settled and Quote all now open on a cased glass with a cursor or tube top right, and five designs share the same To do row (amber 'was due', square tick, NOW rule). The two that stand apart at a glance are Trued (a horizontal line with plates) and Dessau (the poster). Between the camps, the tour lines (Trued, Manual) gained most by taking the main camp's frame devices, while the main lines mostly polished. Amber is still used as an outline and ring colour on Quote, Dessau and Departures; it should be ink for 'late' only. The phosphor halo is back where it belongs on most designs (the lit word, the tubes, the leader). Dessau's welcome wash is the one place it spreads into glare.

scores.why: The most finished system in the heat. The box is unboxed and moved to a rule head, the plates hang on leaders and carry a real second fact (the drive from home), the 'Around the house' yard folds setup into one lamp, and the status foot repeats on every page. The rail is lit only from now to the next stop. Faults: the plates are still graphite boxes on a page that says 'no boxes', and at rest the foot has no lamp on Plans, To do or Settings, so those pages lose their one light.

Bringing back the round countdown dial fixed last round's worst fault. Its bezel ticks name the plan days, and the one straight leader dropping onto NOW is the clearest 'light wired to what it reports' in the heat. It also has the richest grounded colour. Faults: the leader runs about 245px down a column with about 150px of dark ground beside it, and the bar menu still numbers its items 1-6 (folio costume).

Tidier than 14a. Square ticks are back, the Lately added rail now runs through both columns and ends in an 'Add an idea' stop, and the patch lead and the on-glass title still hold. Faults: the desk is close to colourless (Coming up is all bone with one green 4), and the month lights every future plan day, which breaks its own 'one light a band' rule.

The boldest page here, and its circles finally draw real data: the 28-day dial puts the days at true angles. Faults I would push on: a radial green wash still floods the top of Home, To do's tube glows amber 'LATE 3' (light used for a warning), and the filled kind squares in seven inks edge toward confetti. The footer shape legend survives, though last round's lesson allowed one per site at most.

The quote screen with a big '1 DAY' and the four-week tape is a strong glance device, and the 'counts are ink, live is light' law is clear. Faults: the setup strip still leads with an amber ring and an amber '3' (a warning costume), To do runs a column of amber edges, the thin coloured figures (wheat 4, violet 12) look like a theme rather than data, and the title is a retired question form.

The wire from the box into the dot-matrix board still has the strongest single gesture in the heat, and the phone board is fixed. Faults: To do's rail now runs about 230px of empty steel to reach the Ready buffer (a stretch fix, which the lessons warned against), the starter rows carry blue, green and yellow edges with no job, it is 69% green, and the title is the weakest here.

Calmer and joined up: the short lead into NOW lands, and the household row has real figures. Faults: the inner pages have turned into a generic dark dashboard (Plans' month is a bare grid, Ideas a plain table), the glass now looks like Desk's, which is convergence, and the wording 'Status 1 of 3 on' reads as a fault.

Still strong. The tube as the line's lit head and the meter are as good as last round's judges said. But the plates are stretched to the rail and it carries 'needs a' in the title, and the cross fixes both.
The patch lead is good. The ring-as-tick on To do, the hole under the kids' wishes and an almost colourless desk hold it back.
Good colour and rails, but the slot-glass equaliser on Home is a tall, half-empty dark box with 10px numerals.
The wire and the board are good, and Home is less stretched than in the cross. Still greyish, the green hover competes with the wire, and the ring stops on form fields read as radio buttons.
The figure-led heads are clear. The household row and the amber setup rings were pasted across from Settled, and Coming up has no light of its own.
'plan.' is stranded on its own VT323 line as a broken sentence, and the steel cords beside every figure are ornament.
Bold poster, but drained to 88% green, the waypoint rings sit on bearings that mean nothing, and every link is underlined.
The Matrix complaint stands: green on green everywhere, glare instead of hierarchy, the same tube treatment on every element, and no grounded colour.
The cased terminal is a real idea, but the page beside it is a stack of boxes, and 'What's on your mind?' fails as the box's label.
A good track grammar, but the plates are boxes over the rail and the setup strip uses the ring language a second time without the same meaning.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the leader-hung plates, the drive fact, the 'Around the house' yard with setup folded into the Settings stop, and the lit run from now to the next stop. Fix: (1) Coming up: drop the plates' graphite fill and frame and let the name, the time well and the drive sit on the ground over their leaders, so the only frames on Home are the greeting and the tube. (2) Status foot: at rest, give the lamp a dim steady phosphor core (not breathing), so every page keeps one live light; keep the breathing state for 'Answering'. (3) Lately added: the kind rings are all steel-cyan, so give each kind word its grounded ink (sage, wheat, clay) at low chroma so the column is not monochrome. (4) Between 48rem and 75rem, let the yard wrap to two rows of stops rather than wrapping each stop's facts under its name.

Keep the dial (bezel ticks with numerals, the sage free-weekend arc, the hot NEXT IN figure), the straight leader onto NOW, the dimmed 1px NOW traces, the readout strip and the rail with kind words for Lately added. Fix: (1) Shorten the leader. Move the dial down so it sits in the Coming up column head (its socket about 60-90px above NOW), and put the NEXT PLAN caption beside it, which also fills the 150px of dark ground. (2) Take the numbered 1-6 circles out of the bar's Settings menu. (3) Status: drop the 'FIG. 1' caption so captions follow one rule across pages. (4) Ideas: the readout's Nearest and Furthest are good; cut the radar's share so the page falls under about 70% green.

Keep the case and the patch lead into NOW, the title on the glass with one block cursor, the Lately added rail through both columns ending in 'Add an idea', and the square ticks. Fix: (1) Colour the desk. Coming up's month and weekday captions in wheat or dusk at real chroma, and the kind words in Lately added as grounded inks (they partly are already; extend the same to the To do 'who' column and the Status bands). (2) Month view: light only the next plan's numeral, and give the later plan days a steel underbar, so the 'one light a band' rule holds. (3) Move the 'Give Vera something to plan.' prompt above Next up on the glass (usability's note from 14a), so the prompt is read before the tube's data.

Keep the poster type, the 28-day dial with days at true angles, the readout strip and the per-page round tube that draws its own data. Fix: (1) Remove the radial green wash behind the title and dial on Home: the halo on 'plan.' and the lit rim are light enough. (2) To do's tube: say 'LATE 3' in bone on the glass with a small amber triangle, never as amber glow, because light is phosphor and warnings are ink. (3) Drop the footer shape legend; let the shapes explain themselves on a help page. (4) Kind squares: cut them to 8px in muted inks, or outline them only, so seven colours do not shout down the Lately added column.

Keep the quote screen with the big days figure, the THEN line and the four-week tape, and the 'counts are ink, live is light' law. Fix: replace the amber ring and amber '3' in Finish setting up with a steel ring and a bone figure, keeping amber only for late rows; drop the amber left edge on late rows to one amber dot beside the date so To do is not a warning column; change the title to an instruction (see titles); and put the figures in bone and dusk with only the live one lit, not wheat, violet and cyan.

Keep the wire from the box's ring into the board and the board with its clock and trace. Fix: (1) End To do's rail at its last row, and put the Ready lamp in a page-wide foot (as Trued does) rather than stretching a rail through 230px of empty ground. (2) Make the starter rows' coloured left edges one steel colour, or give each the section ink of its destination together with that page's icon, and say so. (3) Retire 'headed'.

Keep the short lead into NOW, the household row with figures and the glass status line. Fix: give the inner pages back the rack tubes that made this line itself (Plans' 'this weekend' leaf, a To do tally tube on every page, not only a few), make the glass look different from Desk's (the videotex grid, mosaic heads), and reword 'Status 1 of 3 on' to '1 connected'.

a.titles: Best: 'Tell Vera what to plan.' (Trued). It is short, imperative, names who hears you, and ends on the lit word with the full stop inside the light. Close second: 'Give Vera something to plan.' (Desk, on the glass), where 'something' covers reminders and wishes. 'Hand Vera anything to plan.' (Manual) is acceptable, but 'hand ... to plan' is a little stiff. 'Send Vera anything to plan.' (Settled) makes it sound like mail. 'Tell Vera. Let's plan.' (Dessau) is better than 'she'll plan' because it makes it a joint effort, but two sentences read as a slogan and do not work as the box's label. Fails: 'What should Vera plan?' (Quote) is a retired question form, a family can answer 'nothing', and it reads as asking the page to show something. 'Tell Vera where we're headed.' (Departures) narrows the job to trips: a reminder to call the dentist is not where anyone is 'headed', and the metaphor is doing the job's work.

b.notes: The crosses beat their carried parents in every line, most clearly in the tour camp. Sill, Waypoint and Pocket each took the main camp's discipline (unboxed rule heads, one type system, a footer status line, grounded kind colours) and kept their own line drawing, which is exactly what the owner praised in Signal Box. Features that worked: Waypoint's patch lead and Pocket's tube lead (light that visibly lands on the row it reports); Sill's status line on the box's glass (taken from Folio); Folio's Fastext keys (taken from Waypoint's readout) in grounded inks; Pocket's tabbed 'At the back' strip; Plate's channel concept. Features that read pasted: Plate's square-root dial plus a separate 30-day trace on Status (two instruments competing); Folio's slide-rule spend meter sitting alone in a wide column; Listing's thread across the setup strip (too faint to read as one rail). The main-camp lines (Plate, Listing, Folio) are calm and well typeset but carry less line art and less glow; the tour lines carry the owner's favourite structure and, after crossing, are as calm. Glow: all keep #6dff9c halos on the lit word, Send and tubes. Sill and Waypoint place the light best; Plate's grey plate mutes it. No candidate breaks the floors, though Pocket's three small Home targets need fixing.

scores.why: The original glow is all there, but it is everywhere: a monochrome green wash, boxed panels and no structure. It is still 'the Matrix', which is what the owner asked to move away from.

A calm and well-built desk terminal with a good lit tube, but it is grey-boxed and has little line art. Its Home sections are panels, not tracks, so it reads closer to a generic modern dark UI than the owner wants.
Strong track language: the Coming up rail with its lit Now run, the ways-to-start branch and the To do rail. The squares and the grey slate panels still box the page a little.

The engraved plate and the bevelled tube read as a real instrument, and the brass labels are a nice grounded note. But the page is mostly flat slate bands with little line art leading the eye, and Home's lower half is busy.

The channels are the right idea: a lit groove from Now to Next, To do's amber late stretch meeting a lit NOW, and Status's dial feeding a groove over the lamps. The 'lands in' plate keys are a good touch. But the whole page sits on one lighter slate plate, which flattens the black and the glow, and the Coming up glass is small and cramped.

The head-column listing is orderly and the stem from tube to NOW is a good gesture. It is cool and grey with little colour beyond the green, and the bands read as a spreadsheet more than a lit programme guide.

The dropped stem onto a breathing NOW, the one thread on to To do's NOW and the sage pulses are honest and calm. The head column with its big figures is good typesetting. It lost some glow and personality: below the tube it is mostly hairlines and grey.
The teletext contents page has character, and the glow on 'on' and the tubes is real. But the inner pages' 9xx numbering clutters them, and Home is dense, with two radars.

The lit Row 0 on dark glass with a white-hot page number is a fine CRT device, and so is the Fastext row of grounded section-ink keys. Fraunces figures with real caps give the best typesetting in the heat, and the Contents list is a nice wayfinder. The serif and the bone colour lean bookish, and Status's left column is thin.

The question stands on a lit week: the tube on the rail with plates and a lit run to stop one. The branch of ways to start and the progress dots are good. The To do and Lately boxes are still boxed slabs, and the lamp-key footer rail is decorative.

The heat's best line language. The tube's power lamp drops a lit wire onto stop one, every plan is one plate on a post over its ring, every list below hangs from its own short track with a ring head and a T foot, Chat hangs from one track, and the foot is a status rail. The glow is concentrated on 'plan', the wire and the box's status line, and the plates take grounded kind colours. Faults: the posts are long and empty, and the steel-on-slate plates are a little uniform.
One steel line of time with rings, diary-set dates and good typography. But the right-column boxes (To do, wishes, eat) fight the line, and the title's 'pencil' is a weaker word for the job.

Bound well. One lit line from Now to Next lands on Coming up's Next row, a short lead drops from the tube onto 'tomorrow', the Due/Later stops have the amber due lamp, and diary numerals lead every row. 'At the back' tabs in muted sage, steel, wheat and violet are a lovely touch of grounded colour, and the content is unboxed. Weak points: the phone bar loses the FamilyDB word, three targets under 44px on Home, and the box's lit wash is large.
The route with waypoint rings carrying the day numerals is a distinctive line drawing, and the readout strip is crisp. The tube is small and the lower page is plain.

The patch lead from the Next row to the tube's socket is the clearest 'light goes somewhere' in the heat. The route arcs ring 4/9/17/24, the annunciator readout is beautifully ruled with an amber Late, kind ticks in grounded colours sit on Lately, and the month strip repeats the route. The glow is right on 'plan.', Send and the tube. Below Coming up the page thins out into plain rules (the kids' wishes band is an empty line), and Status loses its lamp board.

fixes.suggestion: Keep: the wire from the tube's lamp to stop one, the plates on posts, one short-track rule for every list (ring head, rail, T foot, one lamp), the chat track and the status-rail foot. Fix, Home: shorten the posts (lift the rail, or give the ink plates a second line such as kind and who, so they are fuller and nearly as tall as plate one). Give each plate a 2px top cap in its kind's grounded colour so the four are not all steel. Move 'All plans' onto the rail's end tick. To do: the kids'-wishes row hangs oddly off the To do track; give it its own short track or a rule head. Status: carry a lit groove from the meter to the working lamps, as Plate did. Plans month: keep the NOW run and use the kind dots on every event. Phone: show a second starter key clearly (no partial key), and put 'Send where I am' inline as Pocket did.

Keep: the route arcs with numeral rings, the patch lead from the Next row to the tube, the ruled annunciator readout with its amber Late, the coloured kind ticks, and the jewel-means-Now rule. Fix: carry the line language below Coming up. Give To do a vertical leg (rings at the late items, lit NOW) and give the kids' wishes band real rows or fold it into a line, since an empty band reads unfinished. Status: bring back a lamp board or rails with lit stops; the three columns are just lists. Ideas: hang the log from the radar with a lead to the nearest row, as Home does. Give the hero glass a touch of scanline over the title so the CRT reads beyond the tube.

Keep: the bound steel line with Now/Next/Due/Later stops, the lead from the tube to the Next row, the diary numerals, the 'At the back' tabs in muted inks, and the unboxed rule heads. Fix: restore the FamilyDB word in the phone bar, and bring Home's three under-44px targets up to size. Dim the box's lit wash a step so 'plan.' and Send carry the light. Fix the Plans lit run for a next plan in a later week. Give the right column (kids' wishes, eat) a short stub off the line so it belongs to the spread.

Keep: the lit Row 0 with the white-hot page number, the Fastext keys in grounded inks, the Contents list and the Fraunces figures. Fix: hang Plans and To do from the steel rail with ring stops (not just dots), so the line art reaches Home. Status: fill the left column, or give the slide rule the full width with the Waiting list beneath. Pull the bone a step cooler so the serif feels like a terminal's magazine, not a print book. Phone: get Plans onto the first screen.

Keep: the channel idea (grooves lit only Now to Next), the round dial feeding the lamp groove, and the 'lands in' plate keys. Fix: put the page back on near-black and keep the slate plate for the cut instrument areas only; the global grey plate flattens the glow. Make Coming up's glass larger and drop the per-row lit drop's 47px indent so the rows line up with Lately.

Keep: the stem from tube to NOW and the one thread to To do's NOW, and the head column with figures. Fix: add a little more phosphor life (a scanline on the tube's trace, glow on NOW) and some grounded colour in the head column's figures or icons. Fill the empty glass at the trace's right end.

b.titles: Best: Sill's 'What needs a plan? Tell Vera.' It names the job (anything that needs arranging), says who hears you, and lights a short word that sits over the lit run that answers it. Close behind: Pocket's 'Jot it down for Vera to plan.', which is warm, in the diary's own voice, and makes the act plain. Waypoint's 'Send Vera anything to plan.' is clear and inviting, though 'send' is a little mechanical. Plate's 'What should Vera plan?' is fine but passive: it asks the family to decide, not to hand over. Listing's 'Put it on Vera's list.' undersells the job (a list, not plans and reminders acted on). Folio's 'Tell Vera what's on.' is the weakest: the lit 'on.' is a tiny, vague word that does not say planning, and it reads close to the rejected 'What's on your mind?'.

b.notes: Through the soul lens every cross beat its carried parent, and all by the same mechanism: light now goes somewhere. Grafts that took: Sill Line's stem/wire principle, now native in four lines (sill's tube wire, listing's straight stem, pocket's lead, waypoint's patch lead, plate's channel). Joined's meter, as plate's round dial and folio's slide-rule glass. Folio's glass status line, rebuilt on Sill's box as 'Vera is listening' with a cursor. Waypoint's readout strip, as folio's Fastext keys. Grafts that read pasted: plate's flush starter keys (a table under the box), pocket's 'At the back' tabs (pleasant but a different site's device), and listing's sage pulses, which leave the month without a lit today. The camps have converged: the tour lines bring the wiring, the main lines the glass heads. The best of this heat (sill, folio) join both. Risk: four of six now draw a NOW rail with a lamp on To do. Keep each line's signature as its lit object (sill's wire, folio's Row 0 glass, plate's channel and dial, waypoint's route rings) so the field stops looking alike. Waypoint at 38% green is grounded, but its inner pages drift toward lifeless. Phosphor should remain at one device per page.

scores.why: Has the tube's light everywhere (halo, bloom, the Matrix wash), but because it is everywhere it says nothing: glare, not attention. The soul is there but it has no structure.
The title typed on the glass with a block cursor is still the most tube-like greeting. But the rest of the page drained to near-colourless slate, and below the case the light has nowhere to go.
The lit week rail and plates give the phosphor a job, and it is calm. The plates are stretched over dead graphite, and the tube sits in the row rather than leading it.
The cut plate is a real instrument idea, and the screen behind it is at the original's full strength. The stencil leak under 'plan' reads as an underline, and 69% green weighs the lower page.

The channel finally lets light travel: the slot's Now drops to the Next row, and To do's NOW crossing with a pinhole is right. Status's round square-root dial feeding the lamp groove is the best Status soul in the heat. The flush starter keys under the box are heavy, and the 13:00 node collides with the time.
Its stem from the tube is the line's best idea, but the stem is a long right-angled jog across empty ground, and the filled slate bars mute the listing.

The stem now drops straight from the tube onto a breathing NOW and tapers: honest, lit wiring. But the month lost its lit today, Status's dial shrank to a token, and below Coming up the page is a printed listing with little light left.
The halo'd 'on' on scanlined glass with its status line is among the most CRT-souled greetings, and the radar and NOW rails are lit with purpose. The 'What's on for us?' label fails as an invitation.

The tube lives here: Row 0 on dark glass with a white-hot page number, the title typed on scanlined glass with a lit 'on.' and cursor, To do's own 'Open, by when' glass, and a slide-rule spend glass. The Fastext keys are grounded and the rest of the page is a calm magazine. Fraunces in bone on the glass is a little bookish for a tube.
The lit sill from now to stop one gives the greeting a live line. But Lately and To do are boxed beneath it, and the legend rail is an empty strip.

The most alive and the most disciplined at once. The tube's power lamp drops a lit wire onto stop one, the run from the breathing now lamp is the only bloom, the box carries a glowing status line ('4 plans · 3 late · Vera is listening') with a cursor, and Status is a real lamp board beside a needle dial. Everything else is grounded slate and wheat.
The lit chain and the warming tube are real, but the right column is boxed main-camp parts, a second tube repeats Next up, and the amber rings read as a warning column.

The line lit from Now to Next with a short lead from the tube to its row is well wired, and the green month glass on Plans is lovely. To do's olive NOW line muddies the 'one lit NOW' rule, the box's green wash is broad, and the phone hides the wordmark.
The route rings carrying numerals and the pool under 'plan.' give a cockpit's light. The right column beside Coming up is empty and Ideas is confetti.

The patch lead from the Next row into the tube and the lit Next ring on the route are wiring done right, and the readout column is a true instrument head. The other pages, though, are mostly unlit lists (To do, Ideas, the Status columns), so at 38% green the tube's light risks going thin away from Home.

fixes.suggestion: KEEP the wire from the tube's power lamp to stop one, the lit run from now (the only bloom), the glowing status line in the box, and Status's lamp board with its dial. FIX: the ink plates are short on long posts. Set each plate's time line as a VT323 readout lit at the dim tier, so the lit run's stops each carry a faint afterglow, or shorten the posts. Lately added's ring lamp is too small: make the newest ring a 6px breathing lamp. On the phone, show the next plate before the starters. Give the Plans month's today cell the lit ring at full bloom, as Home's stop has. Drop the footer lamp key except on Status.

KEEP Row 0 with its white-hot page number, the scanlined title glass with the lit 'on.' and cursor, To do's 'Open, by when' glass, and the slide-rule spend glass. FIX: set the bone title on the glass in VT323 or Plex Mono, or at least warm it as faint phosphor-bone with scanlines over it, so it reads as typed on the tube rather than a printed serif pasted on glass (keep Fraunces for page heads). Status's left column is now only Waiting: move the lamp board (who answers, keys, connected) there as a small glass. Plans' NOW rail needs a lit dot tying it to the radar's '4'.

KEEP the patch lead into the tube, the jewel = now and lit ring = next law, and the readout column. FIX: carry one lit device per page so the phosphor is not Home-only. Put a NOW crossing with a breathing lamp on To do (it has only a flat rule), put the status lamps as lit jewels beside Who answers on Status, and give Ideas' radar row a lit lead to the nearest row. Restore Home's lower half a little warmth: the Lately added bars are plain grey ticks; tint them in the kinds' grounded inks.

KEEP the channel grammar, the round square-root dial feeding the lamp groove on Status, and To do's NOW crossing with its pinhole. FIX: the Next node sits on '13:00' (13:0●); move it into the channel gutter. The flush starter keys under the box read as a heavy table: make them a lighter engraved strip with one hairline. The setup band at full width is a large unlit block above the lists; shrink it to one engraved line with an amber pinhole. Plans' month dial strip is good: give today a full-strength lit pinhole.

KEEP the Now-to-Next lit line, the short lead from the tube to the Next row, and the green month glass on Plans. FIX: To do's NOW line should be phosphor, not olive/amber: amber belongs to the late rings, NOW to the green. Narrow the box's green wash to its top lip. Show the FamilyDB wordmark on the phone. 'At the back' tabs are pleasant; keep them grounded.

KEEP the straight stem from the tube onto a breathing NOW, tapering to sage, and the thread to To do. FIX: give the Plans month back a lit today (a phosphor numeral with the kit's halo, not just the steel reverse). Enlarge Status's dial to carry real weight, or replace it with a slide-rule glass. Lately added and Ideas need one lamp each (the newest row's icon lit). The pulse tube still has 70px of dead glass: let the trace run its width.

b.titles: Best: "What needs a plan? Tell Vera." (sill): a short lit word over the lit run that answers it, and the spoken 'Tell Vera.' fixes last round's missing addressee. Joint best: "Send Vera anything to plan." (waypoint): one clean line, 'anything' takes in reminders and wishes. "Tell Vera what's on." (folio) is the most phosphor setting, typed on glass with a cursor, and works as the box's label far better than "What's on for us?", though 'on' is a vague key word. "What should Vera plan?" (plate) puts the decision on the family and reads as a quiz. "Jot it down for Vera to plan." (pocket) has the diary's voice but runs long. "Put it on Vera's list." (listing) fails: 'list' narrows the job to a to-do list and the lit word is the weakest of the six.

b.notes: The crosses beat their carried designs on every line, by the most on Folio and Listing. Grafts that worked, rebuilt in the receiving line's own terms: Waypoint's readout strip became Folio's Fastext row in grounded inks (native, and the best colour move in the heat); Trued's square-root meter became Folio's horizontal slide rule; Sill's lit stem became Listing's short drop from tube to NOW (now honest and short, closing 14a's wire to nowhere); Desk's patch lead became Waypoint's Next-row lead and Pocket's lead onto 'tomorrow'; Joined's meter and lamp board became Sill's faceplate and Plate's dial-and-groove. Grafts that read pasted: Waypoint's readout stack beside its own title (a generic dashboard column); Folio's glass status line on Sill's box (fine, but not Sill's own); Plate's channel, which is mostly invisible in stills; Pocket's tube still sitting in a main-camp right column. On the camps: the tour lines (Sill, Waypoint, Pocket) bring drawings of the week (posts, arcs, a diary line), while the main lines bring voice and typesetting (Folio's magazine, Listing's printed listing). The best two in the heat, Folio and Sill, each now hold both. Convergence is lower than in 14a: titles are all different, and each line's signature device is visible at thumbnail size. Phosphor is back where it belongs on all six (title word, tubes, NOW, Send), with no glare across the page. Folio's 'glass only' rule is the clearest statement of the owner's 'bright where it needs to be, grounded elsewhere', and it is the one I would make the standard.

scores.why: The original tube light is honest and the halo is lovely, but every surface is the same green on black. It is the Matrix the family named, with no second idea and no mood beyond the costume.
A well-made, calm desk terminal with the title on glass. Beside this heat's crosses, though, it reads as competent steel-and-green with no signature drawing of the family's content.
The lit rail and the plates give the week a real shape. The stretched plates and the boxed lower half leave it looking like a promising first draft next to its descendants here.
The matte machined plate is a genuine mood. But the stencil 'leak', brass placards in oscilloscope units and violet starter notches feel more like props than parts of a system.

The starters as plate keys flush under the box are the most tactile control in the heat, and the Status dial feeding a lit groove over the lamps is a drawing nobody else has. The channels on Home are too faint to read as the line's idea, and the tube still sits in its corner like 14a's.
A clear programme page, but the stem runs a long right angle across empty ground and the lists are filled slate bars, so it reads busier than a printed listing should.

The wide featured-programme tube, with its pulses and a short white-cored stem dropping onto NOW, is one confident lit gesture. Below it the page reads like a calm printed evening listing, and 'Also on' is a quietly lovely index. The tube's right third is empty glass, and Plans and To do are plain.
The serif almanac on graphite was already the field's most literary mood. Page numbers everywhere and 'What's on for us?' kept it in costume.

The most memorable identity in the heat: Fraunces on scanlined glass with one lit 'on.' and a cursor, a teletext Row 0 with a white-hot page number, a Fastext row in grounded inks, a Contents page, and the month set as big serif numerals. Phosphor lives on glass and nowhere else, which is exactly the owner's brief, and it would look like nothing else. It loses a little where Fraunces numerals crowd To do's date column, and on the tall Ideas radar.
A strong signal-box Home and a complete system, held back by boxed lists under the sill and an empty legend rail in every foot.

Plates on steel posts standing on the sill, with the tube as plate one dropping its wire onto stop one, is a beautiful and legible drawing of the week. The chat timeline that ends at 'your turn', and the Status faceplate with its lamp board beside the dial, carry it across pages. The short tracks with T terminators on To do and Lately added are fussy, and the lower half of Home is quieter than the top.
The diary line is a real idea. Main-camp boxes, a second Next tube and amber rings running down the line diluted it.

Now, Next, Due and Later down the margin turn Home into a diary page, and the short lead from the tube onto 'tomorrow' lands honestly. 'At the back', tabbed in sage, slate, wheat and lilac, is grounded colour with a job, and on Plans the week list sits beside a little month glass, which is charming. The tube floats in its right column, the NEXT UP tag looks struck through, and the phone loses the wordmark.
An exact cockpit with the best colour balance in the field. Its empty column beside Coming up and its confetti Ideas page were its faults.

Waypoint arcs over the day numerals, with a patch lead from the Next row into the radar tube, give Coming up a drawn route that is unmistakably this design. Ideas' big road times, the lit 18 min leading, are a lovely typographic move, and the month rings its days. It is the least green and most varied page here, but the readout stack beside the title is a little generic dashboard, and the arcs are thin at a glance.

fixes.suggestion: Keep: the title on scanlined glass in Fraunces with only 'on.' and the cursor lit; Row 0 with the white-hot page number; the Fastext keys with their grounded top bars; Contents; the month in big serif numerals; the OPEN, BY WHEN glass on To do; the slide-rule spend glass. Fix: on To do, set the due dates in Plex tabular with the month in label caps, not Fraunces, which crowds the date column. On Ideas, cut the radar glass to the filter rack's height, as Waypoint did, so the list starts higher. On Status, fill the 'Waiting' column or fold it under the spend glass. Give Restaurant a hue other than amber. On Home, light one Contents lamp (Settings' amber is good; give Status a live green pin only while answering).

Keep: plates on posts over the sill with the tube as plate one; the wire from the power lamp onto stop one; the box's glass status line; the Status faceplate; the chat line ending at 'your turn'. Fix: drop the T terminators and the extra ring on To do's and Lately added's short tracks: one gutter rail with the lit now line is enough. Give the lower half of Home one lamp of its own (Lately added's newest ring lit, larger than 4px). Bring the plates' bodies to about two-thirds of the tube's height so the posts read as a deliberate rhythm, not as stilts. On the phone, show two starter keys before the fade.

Keep: the arcs on Coming up with ringed numerals, the patch lead from the Next row into the tube, the filled jewel for now or today and the lit ring for Next, Ideas' big road times, and the month's ringed days. Fix: make the readout stack beside the title less generic. Set its figures in the route's numeral face and tie Plans to the route with the same ring, or fold it into one row under the box as on the phone. Thicken the arcs to 1.5px with the Next leg lit, so the route reads at a squint. Put Lately added's coloured kind ticks on the same left edge as To do's boxes.

Keep: the wide featured-programme tube, the short stem onto a breathing NOW, the head column with figures, and the printed rows under hairlines with time columns, plus 'Also on'. Fix: fill the tube's right third, so the pulses span the glass, or narrow the tube to its trace. Give Plans and To do a head-column figure with the same lit NOW they have on Home, because Plans is now a bare grid. Let one grounded hue in per band head (sky for Plans, wheat for To do, sage for Ideas) so the page is not all steel under the one green.

Keep: the diary line with Now, Next, Due and Later; the short lead onto 'tomorrow'; 'At the back' with its grounded tabs; Plans' week list beside the month glass; the diary-set dates; the 'Jot it down' title. Fix: put the tube at the head of Coming up's column and drop the floating right column, so the lead is a straight drop. Clear the struck-through look on the NEXT UP tag. Restore the wordmark on the phone. Let the Kids' wishes and Something to eat sit on the line as Later stops, not as a second page.

Keep: the starter keys cut flush under the box, the Status dial feeding a lit groove over the working lamps, the lit windows on the month, and the engraved seams. Fix: make the channel visible on Home. Widen the lit stretch to 2px with the kit halo, and drop it from the tube itself (not only the small slot) onto the Next row. Shrink the Finish setting up band, which takes a third of the first screen, to one engraved line. Give the plate one grounded companion besides amber (brass or sage on the placards and the kind icons).

b.titles: Best: Folio's 'Tell Vera what's on.' set on scanlined glass in Fraunces with a lit 'on.' and a cursor. It is an invitation, it names who hears you, it covers plans, reminders and ideas alike, and its setting is the most beautiful typographic moment in the heat. Close second: Pocket's 'Jot it down for Vera to plan.' It speaks in the diary's own voice, ends on the lit word, and makes the line's metaphor audible. 'What needs a plan? Tell Vera.' (Sill) is a strong headline with a spoken aside, though the two sizes side by side read a little like a subtitle. 'Put it on Vera's list.' (Listing) is fresh and plain-spoken, but 'list' undersells the planning and could be any to-do app. 'Send Vera anything to plan.' (Waypoint) is serviceable but transactional, and 'Send' repeats the button. 'What should Vera plan?' (Plate) fails: it asks the family to set Vera's agenda, reads passive, and has the least voice.

b.notes: System view: this round the crosses are separated less by effects than by whether one rule holds on every page. Waypoint (jewel and ring law, head rows), Sill (one plate grammar and one short-track rule), Folio (Row 0 and the face jobs) and Listing (the head column) each state a rule and carry it to Plans, To do, Status and Settings. Plate and Pocket have strong rules too, but Plate's slab framing and Pocket's oversized hero break their own scales. Grafts that read native: the patch lead and Next tube beside the route on Waypoint, which fixes last round's empty column with content. Folio taking Waypoint's readout as Fastext keys. Sill taking Folio's glass status line into the box. Listing's stem rebuilt as a straight drop plus a faint thread (the best fix of a failed reach in the heat). Plate's square-root dial from Trued and its lamp groove. Grafts that read pasted: Pocket's 'At the back' four tabs feel like Folio's contents in a different coat; Plate's starter keys flush to the box are fine but echo Listing; Sill's setup ring strip is still the same strip as on other lines (convergence). The camps have met. Every top design now pairs a tour grammar (a route, a sill, a line, a rail) with a main-camp frame (head rows, rule heads, a foot), and the differences are in execution. Convergence risk remains: NOW rails and setup ring strips appear on almost every page. Each line should keep its signature (Waypoint's route, Sill's posts, Folio's Row 0, Listing's thread, Plate's channel, Pocket's line) and drop the shared parts that blur them.

scores.why: Monochrome glow everywhere, boxes inside boxes, no type steps or rules that hold from page to page. It is the yardstick for the light, not for the system.
A sound frame (the case, rule heads, the meter), but the lists are boxed slabs and nothing ties the tube to its rows. Next to this heat it looks like a set of parts more than a grammar.
It has a real grammar (rail, NOW, plates) and calm grounded colour. The plates float on empty graphite, and the lower half of Home has no system of its own.
Engraved seams and the day numeral are a consistent material language. The stencil leak, the placards and the one slab that frames every page make it read as costume more than rules.

The channel is written once as a token with three states and reused on Coming up, To do, Status and Settings, which is real system work. Status's dial, 30-day glass and lamp groove are the richest instrument in the heat. Still slab-on-slab, 69% green, and the hung Coming up rows break the left edge they share with Lately.
The head-column band grid is a strong layout rule. The stem was a right-angled jog to nowhere, and the lists were filled bars.

The head column (h2, figure, links) now holds on Home, Ideas, Plans, To do and Status. The stem drops straight onto NOW and threads faintly through the setup strip to To do's NOW, which closes the line's failed reach. 'Also on' turns the tail of Home into contents lines. Weak spots: Plans month drops the head column's lamp, and the whole page leans on one green.
Contents lines and NOW rails are a clear system. Page numbers in the nav and synthesized small caps were costume.

Row 0 is a true system device: the same glass header line on every inner page, with page numbers only where teletext put them. The three faces have clear jobs, Fastext keys tie colour to sections, and To do's 'Open, by when' glass and Status's slide-rule meter are well built. Restaurant in amber breaks the late-only rule, and Status's left column is thin.
The most complete system last round (faceplate, rule heads, square ticks). To do and Lately were still boxed, and there was a long empty legend rail.

One plate grammar (kind ring, name, numeral and time) on the tube, the plates, the phone and the Plans list. One short-track rule (gutter rail, ring at the head, a T foot, one lamp) under every list below the sill. The Ready foot is on every page and the boxes are gone from the lists. The posts are long under short plates, and the setup strip's amber rings still read slightly as a warning.
The one line of time is a good page-wide rule. The boxed right column and the amber ring column fought it.

The line now runs down every page, Chat included, and ends at an honest 'Answering' terminus. The tube's lead lands on its own row, the pages are unboxed, and 'At the back' tabs give grounded colour a job. Three small targets slipped back in, the hero title is very large against an otherwise quiet system, and To do's Now rule turns olive.
The numeral law and the four keyed shapes are very coherent. It left an empty right column on Home and a confetti Ideas page.

Each hole is filled with content. The annunciator stack meets the box's top and foot, the tube sits beside the route with a short patch lead into its Next row, and the jewel means Now, the ring Next, on Home and the month alike. Whose became a latched segment, Ideas leads with nearest first, and the green share is the lowest in the field (39%). The 'Ideas 12' and 'Things to do 4' head rows are the cleanest type scale here. Minor: the stray tick bars before the kinds in the Ideas log and on Lately, and a slightly airy readout.

fixes.suggestion: Keep: the patch lead from the Next row into the tube, the jewel and ring law, the annunciator stack, the head rows ('Ideas 12' with its unit), the latched Whose segment and the Ready foot. Fix: drop the coloured vertical tick before each kind on the Ideas log and Lately added; the kind's icon and hue already say it, and the bars read as stray selection marks. Tighten the readout rows to about 52px and let the box grow, rather than stretching the rows. Give The kids' wishes on Home a body (two name rows with their lamps), not just a head row with an empty band under it. On Status, put the needle's 30-day ghost inside the glass as on Trued.

Keep: the one plate grammar, the lit wire from the tube to stop one, the short-track rule under every list, and the Status faceplate. Fix: shorten the posts. Either top-align the ink plates and raise the rail under them, or add a third line to each plate (the place, or who it is for) so the posts are about 24px. Set the setup strip's step rings in steel, with amber only on the warning glyph. On the phone, show a second starter's full label, or wrap the starters to two rows.

Keep: Row 0 on every inner page, the three faces with jobs, the case with its glass title, the Fastext keys, the contents lines and To do's 'Open, by when' glass. Fix: move Restaurant off amber (wheat or terracotta) so amber means only late. Fill Status's left column, by putting the lamp board under Waiting or moving Waiting under the meter. On Ideas, bring the radar down to the filter's height. On Home, drop the Fastext tallies' coloured caps or key them to the section inks used in the Contents.

Keep: the head column on every band, the stem dropped straight from the tube onto NOW, the faint thread to To do's NOW, the leader rows, and 'Also on'. Fix: Plans month should carry the same thread (today's cell lit, a lit run to the next plan) so the rule holds there too. Give the Next up tube's empty right glass the plan names on the bars. Add one grounded companion hue to the head-column figures (bone or steel) so the page is not all green and grey.

Keep: the channel token (groove, lit and unlit states) and its use on To do's late stretch, the Status dial-to-lamp groove, and the month's numeral windows. Fix: drop the outer slab on inner pages (Ideas and To do sit in a plate inside the page), and let the seams carry the plate. Line the Coming up rows up with Lately's left edge by moving the channel into the gutter. Tie Settings' pinholes to a real state field rather than to words. Bring green down by dimming the radar bezel and the box's bevel spill.

Keep: one line on every page, the lead from the tube to its row, the 'Answering' terminus and the 'At the back' tabs. Fix: bring the hero title down a step (about 2.75rem) so it sits inside the type scale. Draw To do's Now rule in phosphor, not olive. Restore 44px targets on the three small links. When setup is done, raise the tube to the top of the right page.

b.titles: Best: Sill's "What needs a plan? Tell Vera." The question is the display line and "Tell Vera." works as the box's spoken label, so title and control are one unit, and the lit "plan" sits over the lit run that answers it. Close second: Waypoint's "Send Vera anything to plan.", one clean imperative that names Vera, takes in reminders, ideas and wishes, and keeps the full stop inside the lit run, which is the credited setting. Plate's "What should Vera plan?" is serviceable, but it asks the family to decide for Vera rather than inviting input. Folio's "Tell Vera what's on." finally works as the box's label, and the on-glass setting with a cursor is the most phosphor, but "on" is a thin key word. Listing's "Put it on Vera's list." fails the job: it shrinks FamilyDB to a list keeper, and it is a step down from plans. Pocket's "Jot it down for Vera to plan." has the right voice but is seven words at display size and over-long for a label.

b.notes: Every cross beat its carried design through this lens, and the margins are largest where a graft closed a reading gap. Waypoint's patch lead, taken from Desk's socket idea, fills the right-column hole with the tube and ties it to the Next row: this is the heat's best graft for comprehension. Listing's straight drop, after the 14a lesson, turns a decorative wire into a pointer. Folio's Fastext keys (from Waypoint's readout strip) read native and pressable. Sill's tour-of-Folio status line reads pasted: it was put inside the textarea, where words read as input. Plate's grafted 'starters flush to the box's foot' broke the composer's unity and its Tab order: it is the one cross that regressed on a basic interaction. Pocket took main-camp unboxing and a To do quick-add well, but its crosshair toggle, copied from a messenger's attach key, is unlabelled on the phone, and its focus is nearly invisible. The camps have converged further. Tour lines (Waypoint, Sill, Pocket) bring the clearest at-a-glance time grammars. Main lines (Listing, Folio) bring the best finding aids: head columns, 'Also on' and Contents rows that state each page's condition. The best pages here have both. All six crosses keep 0 to 3 small targets, against today's 42. Remaining common faults: on the phone the next plan often sits at or under the fold (Listing, Folio), starters rows rely on a fade to show they scroll (Sill, Waypoint), and template-side state (Waypoint's ?sort, Plate's word-sniffed lamps) is not backed by data.

scores.why: The eye lands on the green glare first, not on the title. Setup, wishes and Coming up are all boxes of equal weight. 42 of 55 Home targets are under 44px, and To do is a grid of cards with folded disclosures. It is hard to take in at a glance.

The order is clear and there are no small targets. But Next up's glass sits above the title, so the eye reads the plan before the question, and the Tab order goes to the tube's links before the box. Its lists are good but dense, and the lower left is a hole.

The title, box and starters branch read in a clean sequence, and the plates on the rail tell the week at a glance. But on the phone the tube sits below the fold. The plates stretched to the rail leave empty graphite that slows scanning.

The engraved numerals lead every row, and the composer is a clear unit. The stencil leak under 'plan.' reads as an underline or link. The setup band and the placards take attention from Coming up, and the month has 6 small targets.

The rows are calmer, the To do now line is legible, the dial on Status and the lit lamps are easy to read, and the month events are 44px. But the starter keys now sit between the textarea and From/Send. That splits the composer in two, and the Tab order runs textarea, starters, then select and Send. '13:00' collides with the Next lamp ('13:0●'). The full-width setup band takes the second screen.
The head-column bands are easy to scan, and the figures sit over their labels. But the stem jogs about 500px across empty ground, and the lists are filled slate bars that read as buttons.

This is the most legible Home in the heat. There is one left edge, each band's head column gives its count and links, and the stem drops straight from the tube onto NOW and onto the Next row. The 'Also on' rows tell you where everything else lives, with its state. To do's open boxes are clear. Two costs: it is long, and on the phone the Next up title sits just above the tab bar, with its date below the fold.

The contents lines and rails are a strong finding grammar, with zero small targets. But 'What's on for us?' fails as the box's label. The page numbers in the nav and the see-p400 cross-references add reading cost for a family member.

Page numbers now sit only in Row 0 and Contents, which removes the clutter. The Fastext keys give four figures you can press, and the Plans and To do rails each carry one lit NOW. Contents shows each page's state, which helps finding. But on the phone the case and setup still fill the first screen, the radar's day bearings need a caption to decode, and Status's left column is nearly empty.

It reads question, box, starters branch, then the sill. It has one type system and square ticks. Lately added and To do are still boxed, the legend rail in every footer is noise, and on the phone the week is below the fold.

Every plan is one plate grammar (kind ring, name, numeral, time, how far), and each plate is wholly a link, so the week reads in one sweep. The wire goes from the tube to stop one, and on the phone the whole tube is on the first screen. To do has true column heads. Faults: the status line '4 plans · 3 late · Vera is listening' sits inside the empty textarea and can read as typed or placeholder text. The phone's starters row scrolls with only a fade as its cue. 'All plans' is stranded below the rail, at the far right.
The Now-to-Later line is easy to understand. But Home's right column is boxed, a second Next tube repeats Next up, and the amber rings down the line read as a column of warnings.

The title is now the box's own label, and the lead from the tube lands on 'tomorrow' in the Next row. Home gains a quick-add for To do, which is the fastest path to a common job. 'At the back' tells you where the rest lives. But the 'Where I am' toggle hides its checkbox, and its Tab stop shows almost no focus ring. On the phone it is an unlabelled crosshair. The phone also hides the wordmark. Home, Status and Chat gain small targets (3, 2 and 1, some under 24px).

The readout strip and the numeral law are clear, and the composer is clean. But the right column beside Coming up is empty. Ideas is two columns of tiny squares with 16 small targets, and the Status filter is lost.

This is the clearest scan in the heat. The title, box and starters sit beside a five-row readout that answers 'how are we doing' at a glance. The route's lit ring tops the Next row, and a short patch lead joins that row to the tube that fills the old hole. On the phone the Next line and all four figures are on the first screen. Ideas now starts high and sorts nearest first, and To do's Whose segment latches clearly. Minor faults: the Kids' wishes band is a bare head row, and the footer's shape legend is noise.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the readout beside the hero, the route ring over the Next row, the patch lead to the tube, the phone's Next line with the four figures, the nearest-first Ideas and the latched Whose segment. Fix: give The kids' wishes band its rows (Maya 0 open, Theo 0 open, with the gift ring) or fold it into Lately added's foot, so it is not a bare heading. Drop the footer shape legend, or show it only on Plans. Make the Ideas order switch and To do's Whose segment real server parameters, so they survive a reload and work with scripts off. On the phone the starters row scrolls: add a visible count or a wrap, not only a fade.

Keep the one left edge, the head-column bands, the straight stem from the tube to NOW, the 'Also on' rows with their states, and the open To do boxes. Fix: shorten the phone's first screen. Fold the three starters into one row of compact keys, or put them under Coming up, so that Next up's date and countdown are above the fold. Close the tube's empty right glass by ending the trace at four weeks, or print the plan names on the bars. Bring the Kind heading on the form down to the field-label weight.

Keep the plate grammar (the whole plate is the link), the wire from the tube's lamp to stop one, the column heads on To do and the Status faceplate. Fix: move '4 plans · 3 late · Vera is listening' out of the textarea, onto the box's top lip or under the title. Inside the field it reads as typed text or a placeholder. Move 'All plans' up into Coming up's head row beside '4 coming'. Make Lately's lamp larger than 4px. On the phone, wrap the starters into two rows rather than a snap-scroller.

Keep Row 0, the Fastext figures as keys, the Plans and To do rails with one NOW, and Contents with each page's state. Fix: on the phone, put Plans' first row before the setup strip and shorten the case (title, box, Send), so the next plan shows on the first screen. Caption the radar's bearings, or drop the radar for the plain rail. Fill Status's left column (move Waiting under the spend glass, or set the lamps there). Give Restaurant a hue other than amber.

Keep the title as the box's label, the lead from the tube onto the Next row's readout, the quick-add for To do on Home and 'At the back'. Fix: give the 'Where I am' toggle a visible focus ring on its label when the hidden checkbox has focus, and keep the words 'Where I am' on the phone; an unlabelled crosshair does not say what it sends. Restore the wordmark on the phone bar. Bring the Home, Status and Chat targets to 44px. Explain or drop the red ribbon on the current tab, which reads as an error mark.
